title: Atmos Energy taking extra precautions during outbreak
summary: Atmos Energy is implementing increased safety measures for its employees and the public during the COVID-19 pandemic, emphasizing the importance of natural gas service safety. The company is urging homeowners and contractors to postpone non-essential digging projects and to always call 811 two days prior to any necessary digging to prevent damage to underground utility lines. This initiative aims to protect both workers and customers while maintaining reliable natural gas service for over 3 million customers.

title: Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. completed the spin-off of Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation for $1.3 billion.
summary: Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. successfully completed the spin-off of Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation (BIPC) valued at $1.3 billion on March 31, 2020. This strategic move involved distributing Class A shares of BIPC to existing Brookfield Infrastructure Partners unitholders, with each share being exchangeable for one Brookfield Infrastructure unit. Unitholders received approximately 0.11 BIPC shares for every unit held, and BIPC shares began trading on the TSX and NYSE under the symbol "BIPC".

title: US industrial giant 3M scrambles to meet demand for face masks as coronavirus spreads
summary: 3M, a $32 billion Minnesota conglomerate, is significantly ramping up its N95 face mask production to meet unprecedented global demand caused by the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to double its annual production from 1.1 billion to 2 billion within 12 months, a move expected to add $300 million in sales, though this is a small fraction of its overall $32 billion business. Despite the increased production, analysts note that the importance of face masks has focused significant attention on the company, whose shares have fallen more than 22% since the start of the year.

title: Williams-Sonoma, Pottery Barn to end false 'made in America' claims, pay $1M: FTC
summary: Williams-Sonoma Inc. and its Pottery Barn unit have agreed to pay $1 million and cease making unsubstantiated "made in America" claims, as announced by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). The FTC found that the company falsely claimed products like Goldtouch Bakeware and Rejuvenation items were entirely made in the U.S. when they were either manufactured elsewhere or contained significant imported components.

title: Big Reversals for S&P 500 ETFs With Exodus From Treasury Darling
summary: Market volatility is causing significant reversals in exchange-traded funds, with the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) seeing a substantial inflow after a previous outflow. Conversely, BlackRock Inc.'s iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF (SHY) experienced a nearly $1.5 billion outflow following five weeks of inflows. These movements highlight investors re-evaluating positions amidst global market swings.

title: Hillenbrand Completes Sale of Cimcool Business to DuBois Chemicals, Inc.
summary: Hillenbrand, Inc. announced the completion of its wholly-owned subsidiary Milacron LLC's sale of the Cimcool business to DuBois Chemicals, Inc. The transaction resulted in approximately $224 million in cash proceeds for Hillenbrand, with potential for an additional $26 million based on future performance. Hillenbrand plans to use the proceeds primarily for de-leveraging activities.

title: General Mills plant employee has presumed COVID-19 case, company says
summary: General Mills announced that an employee at its Cedar Rapids production facility has a presumed case of COVID-19 and is self-isolating. The company has contacted other potentially exposed employees and implemented enhanced cleaning measures and social distancing at the plant. Officials noted that the FDA has not linked coronavirus to food or food packaging.

title: Cedar Realty Trust Announces Plan To Mitigate COVID-19 Impact, Reduces Capital Expenditures
summary: Cedar Realty Trust announced a plan to mitigate the COVID-19 impact by increasing liquidity by $75 million, reducing its quarterly common dividend to $0.01 per share, and dramatically cutting capital expenditures. The company also withdrew its 2020 earnings guidance due to market uncertainty. These measures aim to preserve financial flexibility and respond to the evolving economic landscape.

title: Legg Mason executives slated for huge paydays after company's sale
summary: Legg Mason executives are set to receive substantial payouts following the company's sale to Franklin Templeton. CEO Joseph Sullivan alone will receive over $21 million as part of his "golden parachute" package. This compensation significantly exceeds the salaries of most of Baltimore's highest-paid athletes, highlighting the generous terms of the acquisition for company leadership.

title: New rapid coronavirus diagnostic test can provide results in as little as 5 minutes
summary: Abbott has developed a new rapid coronavirus diagnostic test that can provide positive results in 5 minutes and negative results in 13 minutes, receiving emergency-use authorization from the FDA. The test runs on the company's portable ID NOW platform, already widely available in healthcare settings, and Abbott plans to supply 50,000 tests daily initially. This development aims to significantly speed up COVID-19 testing and aid in quicker diagnosis and treatment decisions.

title: Amarin Says Eicosapentaenoic Acid Levels From Vascepa In Reduce-It® Strongly Correlated With Cardiovascular Outcomes
summary: Amarin Corporation PLC announced that eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) levels from its drug Vascepa in the REDUCE-IT trial showed a strong correlation with cardiovascular outcomes. The company reported an approximate 400% increase in serum EPA levels following Vascepa administration, while DHA levels decreased by 2.9%. This suggests a significant impact of Vascepa on fatty acid levels related to cardiovascular health.

title: Abbott Labs CEO on new coronavirus test launches: 'There's a need for more'
summary: Abbott Laboratories has received federal clearance for two coronavirus tests and is developing more diagnostic devices. CEO Miles White emphasized the continued need for more testing capabilities, even as the company ramps up production of its rapid ID NOW COVID-19 test and another molecular test. Robert Ford, set to take over as CEO, confirmed that Abbott is prioritizing the distribution of rapid tests to frontline workers.

title: Lake Charles Power Station Achieves Commercial Operation
summary: Entergy Louisiana's Lake Charles Power Station has commenced commercial operation ahead of schedule, providing reliable and clean energy to a growing region. This new combined-cycle gas turbine plant is projected to save customers between $1.3 billion and $2 billion over 30 years and significantly reduces carbon dioxide emissions. The project is a key part of Entergy Corporation's strategy to modernize its generation fleet and enhance environmental stewardship.

title: Coherent and exocad collaborate to streamline digital workflows for dentists
summary: Coherent and exocad have partnered to simplify and improve digital workflows for dental professionals. The collaboration involves developing a data interface between exocad’s DentalDB software and Coherent’s DENTAL COCKPIT slicer, enabling more efficient production of metal dental restorations. This integration streamlines the process from design to production, improving compatibility and efficiency for users of both platforms.

title: ADM commits $1 million to fight COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Archer Daniels Midland Co. (ADM) has pledged $1 million to combat the spread of COVID-19, supporting the World Health Organization, local charities, and matching employee contributions. The company's chairman and CEO, Juan Luciano, emphasized ADM's commitment to employee safety, community support, and maintaining agricultural supply chain continuity. Other companies like Cargill and MGP Ingredients are also contributing to the fight against the pandemic.

title: Allstate makes leap into personalized auto insurance pricing
summary: Allstate has launched a new "personalized pricing" option for its Milewise pay-per-mile insurance, allowing auto insurance rates to fluctuate weekly based on driving behavior. This latest iteration of the telematics-based program, first launched in Arizona in September 2019, aims to provide customers with greater control and transparency over their insurance costs. Allstate views this as a significant step in the evolution of telematics within the insurance industry.

title: UAB will collaborate with Altimmune to test a COVID-19 vaccine candidate
summary: The University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) is partnering with biopharmaceutical company Altimmune, Inc. for preclinical testing of its AdCOVID vaccine candidate against COVID-19. This collaboration will involve testing immune responses in mice, a critical step before Altimmune can begin Phase 1 human trials in Q3 of the same year. AdCOVID is a single-dose, intranasal spray vaccine that leverages Altimmune's experience in similar respiratory pathogen vaccines.

title: LifeMax Launches AmMax Bio Following The License Of Worldwide Rights to a Clinical Stage Orphan Asset From Amgen
summary: LifeMax Laboratories, Inc. announced the formation of AmMax Bio, Inc. and an exclusive worldwide license from Amgen for AMG 820, a monoclonal antibody for treating orphan diseases. AMG 820, which has completed Phase I/II clinical studies, will be developed for Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumors (TGCT) and other orphan indications involving CSF-1/CSF-1R biology. This move aligns with LifeMax's focus on developing first-in-class or best-in-class therapies for unmet medical needs in orphan diseases.

title: Qatar Investment Authority Dodges Bullet by Selling Out of Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance Before 2020
summary: This article highlights the Qatar Investment Authority's (QIA) timely divestment from Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance (ARI) prior to 2020. This move proved strategic as ARI's stock experienced significant declines in early 2020, primarily due to credit market turmoil and concerns over commercial mortgage-backed securities during the pandemic's onset. The QIA's decision allowed it to avoid substantial losses, showcasing a prescient investment strategy.

title: BlackRock’s Fink sees global economy recovering steadily from coronavirus hit
summary: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink expects the global economy to recover steadily from the coronavirus outbreak, attributing this to quick actions by central banks and governments in implementing fiscal stimulus. He notes that these measures are more effective now than during typical financial crises and that ETFs played a crucial role in providing liquidity during market stress.

title: B&W Enterprises returns to profitability in 4th quarter, but feels coronavirus impact
summary: Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises Inc. returned to profitability in its fourth quarter of 2019, reporting earnings of $12.4 million compared to a significant loss in the prior year. Despite this improvement, the company still lost money for fiscal 2019 but significantly less than 2018. The Akron manufacturer also indicated that it is being impacted by the spread of the COVID-19 coronavirus.

title: Conduent partners with AWS to assist in Covid-19 response
summary: Conduent Incorporated announced its partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to help public health agencies respond to Covid-19. Their Maven solution was configured to securely engage patients and track coronavirus cases, with Conduent waiving the software license fee for the Maven Covid-19 module until June 30, 2020. This collaboration aims to provide agility and scalability, speeding up implementation for health organizations.

title: Boeing and Delta Air Lines Suspend Dividends
summary: Boeing (BA) and Delta Air Lines (DAL) have suspended their dividends and share buyback programs due to the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Both companies are seeking government aid to shore up capital as the aerospace and airline industries face unprecedented drops in demand. Dividend payments are unlikely to resume before September 2021, aligning with the conditions of the $88 billion taxpayer assistance package for the airline industry.

title: Delta halts Sky Magazine, triggering layoffs at Minneapolis publishing company
summary: Delta Air Lines has stopped carrying its inflight Sky Magazine, which was published by MSP Communications in Minneapolis. This decision has led to layoffs at the Minneapolis publishing company. The move comes as Delta faces significant financial challenges, projecting an 80% revenue decline and losing $50 million daily.

title: BREAKING: Walt Disney Company Senior Executives Take Salary Cuts Due to Unprecedented Disney Parks COVID-19 Closures
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced significant salary cuts for its senior executives in response to the unprecedented financial impact of COVID-19 and the indefinite closure of Disney Parks worldwide. CEO Bob Chapek will have his salary reduced by 50%, while Bob Iger has agreed to forgo 100% of his salary, affecting VPs, SVPs, and EVPs as well. These temporary cuts will remain in effect until the company sees a substantive recovery in its business.

title: A ‘pandemic drone’ to detect coronavirus infections
summary: The University of South Australia is developing a "pandemic drone" in partnership with Canadian company Draganfly Inc. This drone will use specialized sensors and computer vision to remotely monitor temperature, heart and respiratory rates, and detect sneezing and coughing in crowds, aiming to identify potential coronavirus infections. The technology, initially conceived for war zones and natural disasters, is now being adapted to help address the immediate health catastrophe of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. to Sell Investment in Clear Media Limited for US$253 Million
summary: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. announced its agreement to sell its 50.91% stake in Clear Media Limited for approximately US$253 million to Ever Harmonic Global Limited. This sale is part of Clear Channel Outdoor's efforts to increase liquidity and preserve financial flexibility in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The company is also withdrawing its 2020 guidance and implementing various cost-cutting measures.

summary: This article details the compensation of Equifax CEO Mark Begor and other executives for 2019. It highlights that Equifax CEO Mark Begor was Georgia's highest-paid public company CEO in 2018 based on his compensation. The report was published by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.

summary: Entergy's new 980-MW Lake Charles Power Station, a combined-cycle natural gas plant, began commercial operation three months ahead of its scheduled June start. The $872 million project in Westlake, La., will provide cleaner-emitting electricity, supporting system reliability and is projected to save customers between $1.3 billion and $2 billion over its 30-year lifespan. This plant is part of Entergy's strategy to phase out older, less efficient units and improve its generation portfolio.

title: Gunmen kill one, injure six at Freeport mine office in Indonesia
summary: Gunmen attacked an office of PT Freeport Indonesia in Papua province, killing a New Zealand man and wounding six others. Police identified the attackers as an armed criminal group, and the incident occurred in an area where separatists have conducted numerous attacks on the company's nearby Grasberg operation. Mining operations, however, were not immediately impacted.

title: Titan to donate tires for FFA, 4-H antique tractor restoration projects
summary: Titan International Inc. is accepting applications from National Future Farmers of America (FFA) and 4-H student members for its annual antique tractor restoration program. The company will donate Titan- or Goodyear-brand antique tractor tires for accepted projects, continuing a program that has awarded thousands of free tires since 1996. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last.

title: Hexo needs more capital; shareholders to be further diluted
summary: Hexo Corp. released its fiscal second-quarter 2020 results, showing revenue in line with estimates but requiring an additional CA$23.6 million to satisfy fiscal 2020 cash needs. The company plans to raise capital through equity offerings, leading to significant shareholder dilution. This move, while addressing short-term obligations, highlights the challenges Hexo faces in achieving self-funding status.

title: Honeywell to make crucial N95 masks in Phoenix, hire 500
summary: Honeywell International Inc. is opening a new N95 mask manufacturing facility in Phoenix, aiming to hire up to 500 people to meet increased demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. This new plant, along with an existing facility in Rhode Island, will produce masks for healthcare workers and supply 20 million masks to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The company's CEO, Darius Adamczyk, expressed pride in their role in providing essential equipment during the crisis.

title: Jefferies exec dies from coronavirus complications
summary: Peg Broadbent, CFO of Jefferies Group, died from coronavirus complications at age 56. His death marks one of the first among senior Wall Street executives due to the pandemic and highlights the fragility of life. Broadbent helped Jefferies double in size during his tenure, and the company has pivoted its investment banking operations to focus on restructurings and rescue financings in response to the virus.

title: Kroger adjusts pharmacy hours to help seniors, at-risk shoppers
summary: Kroger is adjusting pharmacy hours in Georgia and South Carolina to open at 8 a.m. starting March 30th to better accommodate seniors and at-risk shoppers during the coronavirus pandemic. The company will also install Plexiglas shields at registers, pharmacy counters, and Starbucks counters. This follows previous adjustments to store hours dedicated to seniors and at-risk individuals.

title: Coronavirus leads Burger King, Tim Horton's parent to pay franchisees
summary: Restaurant Brands International (RBI), parent company of Burger King, Popeye's, and Tim Hortons, announced a $70 million cash advance and rebate program for its North American franchisees to help them cope with the financial impact of the coronavirus pandemic. The company is also providing a special bonus for corporate team members, paid sick leave for some employees, and a $40 million support fund for Tim Hortons employees. Additionally, RBI has implemented measures to ensure employee and customer safety and supported healthcare workers during the crisis.

title: Medtronic Publishes Design Specs for Ventilator to Combat Coronavirus
summary: Medtronic PLC announced it is publicly sharing the design specifications for one of its ventilator products, the Puritan Bennett 560, to help combat the demand driven by the coronavirus pandemic. This move allows other companies to rapidly produce urgently needed ventilators. The company plans to release more information, including software code, soon.

title: Vail Resorts CEO donates $2.5 million to help coronavirus-impacted workers, communities
summary: Vail Resorts CEO Rob Katz has pledged $2.5 million to support workers and communities affected by the coronavirus pandemic. This donation will benefit organizations in three Colorado counties and a new initiative by Governor Jared Polis. The move comes as Vail Resorts anticipates a significant financial hit due to early resort closures.

title: Former Nucor CEO went out with record 2019 compensation
summary: Former Nucor CEO John Ferriola received a record compensation package in 2019, boosted significantly by nearly $3.5 million in severance benefits upon his retirement on December 31st. This article, published by the Charlotte Business Journal, highlights the financial details of his exit. Related articles discuss Nucor's performance and previous CEO compensation.

title: Conbipel, controlled by Oaktree Capital Management, asks for receivership
summary: The Italian clothing retailer Conbipel, controlled by Oaktree Capital Management, filed for a composition with creditors on March 18th to the Asti Court. The company is expected to prepare a recovery plan, and Oaktree is seeking new investors, with unions debating if the COVID-19 pandemic or pre-existing difficulties are the primary cause.

title: OSHKOSH DEFENSE AWARDED $346.4 MILLION TO MODERNIZE VEHICLES IN THE US ARMY AND US ARMY RESERVE FHTV FLEETS
summary: Oshkosh Defense, a subsidiary of Oshkosh Corporation, received delivery orders totaling $346.4 million from the U.S. Army Contracting Command – Warren. These orders will facilitate the modernization of vehicles within the U.S. Army and U.S. Army Reserve Heavy Tactical Vehicle (FHTV) fleets, specifically recapitalizing HEMTT and PLS trucks and manufacturing new PLS trailers. This initiative aims to ensure the FHTV fleet continues to support multi-domain operations and combat missions for years to come.

title: Performance Food Group Company Announces Partnerships and Corporate Actions
summary: Performance Food Group Company (PFG) announced new partnerships and corporate actions to reinforce its business during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company has focused on strengthening the food supply chain by partnering with grocery retailers and supporting its existing restaurant customers, while also taking measures to protect its long-term financial position including drawing $400 million from its credit facility and suspending its share repurchase program. PFG emphasizes its adaptability and commitment to emerging stronger from this period.

title: 500 jobs, $23.4 MM in investment > City of Covington, KY
summary: The City of Covington, KY announced that nine economic development projects, representing over 500 new or retained jobs and $23.4 million in new investment, are moving forward with City support. Key projects include the $4.9 million renovation of the Republic Bank building into Class A office space with a rooftop bar, the relocation of Gentis Solutions' corporate headquarters to Covington, and the expansion of STEP CG. Additionally, the City is supporting the restoration of The Monarch Building and awarded five forgivable loans for facade improvements to small businesses.

summary: Resources Connection, Inc. announced that its trading symbol on the Nasdaq Capital Market will change from "RECN" to "RGP" starting April 2, 2020. This change aligns with their trade name, Resources Global Professionals, and requires no action from current shareholders. RGP, a global consulting firm, aims for this symbol to harmonize with its operating company name.

title: Triferic AVNU Approved for Iron Replacement and Hemoglobin Maintenance in Dialysis Patients
summary: The FDA has approved a New Drug Application for Triferic AVNU® (ferric pyrophosphate citrate; Rockwell Medical), an intravenous formulation designed for iron replacement and hemoglobin maintenance in adult patients with hemodialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease. This new formulation allows for direct intravenous infusion, providing an option for clinics where administration through dialysate is not feasible. Rockwell Medical anticipates launching evaluation programs in Q3 2020, with commercial availability to follow.

title: Unit 4 Top Head for Containment Vessel in Place at Vogtle
summary: The Plant Vogtle nuclear power plant in Georgia reached a significant milestone with the placement of the Unit 4 containment vessel top head, marking progress in the two-unit expansion project. This achievement follows the placement of Unit 3's top head a year prior, with the overall construction about 84% complete. The article also highlights the installation of a 300-ton polar crane and the opening of an on-site medical clinic due to the COVID-19 pandemic to ensure worker safety.

title: Sysco lays off, furloughs workers as COVID-19 disrupts operations
summary: Sysco has initiated headcount reductions, including layoffs and furloughs, due to the ongoing disruption of its operations by the COVID-19 pandemic. The company is the largest Houston-based public company outside of the energy industry. This measure comes as various businesses in Texas face economic challenges because of the coronavirus outbreak.

title: Tune In: Hendrix College Student from Conway Competes in ‘Jeopardy!’ College Championship Thursday, April 9
summary: Joe Coker, a junior at Hendrix College from Conway, Ark., will compete in the JEOPARDY! College Championship on Thursday, April 9. The Championship, presented by LendingTree®, is a 10-day special event featuring 15 sharp students, with the winner receiving a $100,000 grand prize and a spot in the Tournament of Champions. JEOPARDY!, hosted by Alex Trebek, is celebrating its 36th season and is the top-rated quiz show on television.

title: Valmont Appoints Avner Applbaum as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Valmont Industries, Inc. announced the appointment of Avner Applbaum as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective March 30, 2020. He will oversee all financial activities and the IT function, succeeding Mark Jaksich who will remain for a smooth transition. Applbaum brings 22 years of financial and operational expertise from publicly-traded and private-equity backed companies in manufacturing.

title: Employee dies in accident at Westlake Chemical in Geismar
summary: An employee died in an accident at Westlake Chemical in Geismar, Louisiana, on Sunday. Operators lost contact with the worker in the polyvinyl chloride unit around 12:10 a.m., and the employee was recovered approximately four hours later. Westlake Chemical expressed its deep regret and extended sympathy to the employee's family, stating that an investigation into the incident will be conducted.

title: SPDR Gold MiniShares ETF Celebrates 2-Years of Growth
summary: The SPDR Gold MiniShares Trust (GLDM) recently celebrated its two-year anniversary, establishing itself as the third-largest physically-backed gold ETF in the U.S. GLDM has attracted significant inflows due to its low expense ratio (0.18%) and competitive share price, appealing to buy-and-hold investors. Despite GLDM's growth, the SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) continues to attract strong inflows, indicating a market for both gold-backed products with different investor appeals.

title: Corning Inc. showcases Valor Glass development, a critical tool for COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Corning Inc. is playing a crucial role in the development of a COVID-19 vaccine by manufacturing Valor Glass vials, which Senator Kirsten Gillibrand praised during a visit to their Big Flats plant. The federal government's BARDA awarded Corning Inc. $204 million to increase production, demonstrating the critical need for a massive supply of vials to support potential vaccines by late 2020 or early 2021. This effort is expected to create 94 new jobs and continues Corning Inc.'s historical involvement in fighting public health threats.

title: 5 Ways Video Monitoring Will Aid in Mitigating Construction Site Risk
summary: This article discusses five ways video monitoring, especially with advanced AI capabilities, can mitigate risks on construction sites. It highlights benefits such as improved risk identification, cost savings, enhanced worker safety, assessment of environmental impact, and increased confidence among contractors and owners. title: Detecting VBA Process Hollowing With Cortex XDR
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has observed advanced VBA activity, specifically VBA-RunPE, which is an implementation of the RunPE technique allowing executables to run from memory in Microsoft Word and Excel to evade detection. Attackers use this process hollowing technique to hide malicious code inside legitimate processes and bypass application whitelisting. Cortex XDR, with its behavioral detectors and the latest Agent 7.2, provides protection against VBA-RunPE by identifying anomalous behavior like suspicious command-line arguments and unusual DLL loads by Office processes.

summary: CoreLogic faced a dramatic and hostile takeover attempt in 2020 by Senator Investments and Cannae Holdings, led by Cannae Chair Bill Foley, who also chairs CoreLogic competitor Black Knight. summary: Over a decade ago, Delta Air Lines planned a significant expansion into Africa, announcing eight new routes. Today, only a few of these original routes remain, with passengers often connecting through European partners for other African destinations.

summary: A power outage on Christmas morning affected over 4,000 Evergy customers in Shawnee and Overland Park. The outage, reported at 4:30 a.m., had some power restored, and a crew was on-site making repairs, with full restoration expected by 6 a.m. The cause of the outage was not immediately determined.

title: US adhesives maker buys out Kenya’s Continental Products
summary: HB Fuller, a US-based adhesives and sealants manufacturer, has acquired Kenya's Continental Products Ltd for an undisclosed sum. This strategic move aims to expand HB Fuller's presence in emerging markets and enhance its reach in East and Central Africa by leveraging Continental's distribution network and manufacturing capabilities. Continental's founder, Alfred Lenana, will remain as CEO, and the acquisition follows a long-standing partnership between the two companies.

summary: Institutional interest and investment are driving Bitcoin's current rally, unlike the 2017 surge that was primarily retail-driven. Major players like Paul Tudor Jones and MassMutual are investing in Bitcoin, contributing to its significant price increase alongside other hard assets reacting to the Fed's monetary policy. The article also touches on potential cryptocurrency-related IPOs from Coinbase and Robinhood, reflecting a broader trend of businesses entering the public market, particularly in tech.

title: End of era for film as Kodak gives way to digital imaging
summary: Eastman Kodak has announced the discontinuation of its iconic Kodachrome color film after a 74-year run, due to declining sales amid the rise of digital imaging technologies. The company, which now generates about 70 percent of its revenue from digital businesses, made the "difficult and tough" decision as Kodachrome sales represent less than one percent of its total still-picture film sales. This marks the end of an era for a film that captured many historical moments and was a staple for the Baby Boom generation's family slide shows.

title: Lands' End Q3 FY20: revenue $360 mn; net income $7 mn
summary: Lands' End reported a 5.9% revenue growth to $359.9 million in its third quarter for FY20, ending October 30, 2020, with net income rising to $7.1 million. The company attributed its strong performance to data analytics investments, leading to growth in new customers and high retention rates, despite Covid-19 challenges. Global e-commerce revenue saw a significant boost, and Lands' End successfully launched products on Kohls.com, with plans for further expansion in 2021.

title: Junichi Hanzawa, MUFG’s next banking unit chief, targets Asia for growth
summary: Junichi Hanzawa, the incoming president of MUFG Bank Ltd., a unit of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc., has announced a strategy to prioritize growth in Asia. While focusing on expansion in Asian markets, Hanzawa also indicated potential cutbacks in developed markets like Europe and the U.S. due to low interest rates impacting profitability. He is set to replace Kanetsugu Mike on April 1.

title: TransUnion credit bureau sets up new scoring system
summary: TransUnion, formerly CRB Africa, launched a new credit scoring system in Kenya that provides reports for over five million borrowers. The system, developed using data from various lenders, aims to reduce arbitrary blacklisting and improve lending practices. It assigns scores between 1 and 1,000, allowing lenders to better price products and compete for prime customers.

title: Cargo thefts spike during pandemic as thieves target toilet paper, hand sanitizer, masks
summary: Cargo thefts significantly increased during the first 10 months of 2020, rising 35% compared to the previous year, with spikes in April, May, and June. The surge in thefts targeted essential items like toilet paper, personal protective equipment, and food, driven by the black market demand created by the COVID-19 pandemic. Thieves stole everything from truckloads of paper goods worth up to $40,000 to medical gloves valued at $1 million and even ventilators destined for COVID-19 patients.

title: Introducing the New WisdomTree Enhanced Commodity Strategy Fund
summary: WisdomTree has revamped its commodity investment strategy with the new Enhanced Commodity Strategy Fund (GCC), featuring a lower expense ratio, a 40-act investment structure, and a dynamic maturity selection to optimize returns and reduce volatility. The fund offers broad, diversified exposure to 25 commodities, with overweight allocations to precious and industrial metals to hedge against inflation and capture growth from emerging technologies, while underweighting speculative traditional energy sources. This updated approach aims to provide investors with a robust commodity exposure in a potentially inflationary environment.

title: Eversource close to restoring power to customers across the state
summary: As of Saturday afternoon, Eversource was nearing full power restoration in Connecticut after a Christmas Eve storm, with only 529 customers remaining without power, primarily in Sherman and Bethel. The company had previously restored power to over 44,000 customers and anticipated substantially complete restoration by 8 p.m. that Saturday. Eversource CEO Jim Judge acknowledged the challenging timing for the holiday and praised the efforts of crews, including those brought in from New Hampshire and Massachusetts.

title: Is Walmart open on Christmas Day 2020?
summary: Walmart was closed on Christmas Day (December 25) in 2020, with most stores having closed by 6 p.m. on Christmas Eve and reopening at 7 a.m. on December 26. The article also details Walmart's extended holiday return policy, including a new Carrier Pickup by FedEx program and simplified in-store and online return processes.

title: 530-Foot-Tall Tower Awaits Construction at 3001 John F. Kennedy Boulevard in University City, West Philadelphia
summary: A 34-story, 530-foot-tall skyscraper is proposed for 3001 John F. Kennedy Boulevard in University City, West Philadelphia, as part of the Schuylkill Yards development. Designed by Practice for Architecture and Urbanism and developed by Brandywine Realty Trust, the building will feature a distinctive staggered massing and red aluminum cladding. Construction is projected to begin in mid-2023 and possibly finish in 2026, despite no visible progress at the site as of a December 2020 visit.

title: Caesars Southern Indiana Acquired by Cherokee Tribe
summary: Caesars Southern Indiana casino in Elizabeth has been acquired by the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians for $250 million, following Caesars Entertainment Inc.'s merger with Eldorado Resorts Inc. The tribe will continue to use the Caesars brand and has entered a long-term lease agreement with VICI Properties Inc. for the real estate. The transaction is expected to close in Q3 2021, pending regulatory approvals.

This technology efficiently utilizes Wi-Fi networks by consolidating functions that were previously handled by multiple devices into its software. The company aims to expand its business into various fields like smart factories and construction, addressing the needs for robust and cost-effective wireless network solutions.

title: Extra Space Storage employees donate over 91,000 meals to Utah Food Bank
summary: Extra Space Storage employees in Salt Lake City raised over $22,000 during a virtual food drive for the Utah Food Bank, equivalent to more than 91,000 meals. The company matched employee donations up to $10,000. This initiative helped the Utah Food Bank meet increased demand due to the coronavirus crisis, building on its mission to fight hunger in the state.

title: Air Canada Boeing 737-8 MAX suffers engine issue
summary: An Air Canada Boeing 737-8 MAX aircraft experienced an engine issue shortly after takeoff from Arizona, necessitating a diversion to Tucson. The incident, which occurred on December 22, involved the pilots shutting down one engine after receiving a left engine hydraulic low pressure indication. Boeing did not immediately comment on the event, which happened a month after the U.S. lifted its 20-month flight ban on the 737 MAX.

title: Aerospace giant’s convict CEO could pose threat to firm’s IPO plans
summary: The CEO of Italian aerospace giant Leonardo S.p.a., Alessandro Profumo, has been convicted of fraud and faces a six-year prison sentence, potentially jeopardizing the IPO plans for its US subsidiary, Leonardo DRS. Despite calls for his resignation, Leonardo has stood by Profumo, arguing the conviction is unrelated to his current role and not yet final. This situation is causing concern amongst investors and US defense officials, with experts suggesting it could significantly impact the US listing due to reputational risks and disclosure requirements.

Jeppe Storm will lead the new office while maintaining his role as Vessel Manager for Wind Osprey.

summary: This article examines the demographic trend of emerging markets getting "old before rich," similar to China. title: GM Opens 3D Printing Center for Parts
summary: General Motors has opened a new 15,000-square-foot Additive Industrialization Center (AIC) to advance 3D printing technology in the automotive industry. This facility houses 24 3D printers and will be used for functional prototypes, manufacturing tools, and eventually production parts for vehicles. The AIC aims to accelerate product development, reduce costs, and increase agility in GM's manufacturing processes.

title: KGI fined NT$3.36m over trader’s death
summary: The Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) fined KGI Securities Ltd NT$3.36 million for poor internal control and lax management following the alleged suicide of a stockbroker who secretly managed clients' funds. The broker, Lai, reportedly traded futures illegally for 12 clients, involving at least NT$9.53 million, with his manager failing to supervise his activities properly. This penalty is the highest ever levied against a securities firm in a single case in Taiwan.

title: Yutong Group Invests $200 Million in WeRide
summary: Yutong Group has strategically invested $200 million in WeRide, a leading Chinese Level 4 autonomous driving mobility company, marking it as the largest autonomous driving investment by a Chinese automaker. This partnership aims to advance the application of autonomous driving technology in commercial vehicles like minibuses and city buses. WeRide and Yutong will collaborate on R&D, vehicle platforms, and mobility services to promote the large-scale commercial use of fully driverless vehicles.

summary: WesBanco has provided a $100,000 endowment to West Liberty University (WLU) to establish its first endowed professorship. This fund will support the hiring of an American studies expert and will be added to the Kenneth B. McMillen Fund. WLU and WesBanco hope to expand the endowment to $500,000 and establish more endowed professorships in the future.

title: Residents ‘Appalled’ As IFF Suggests It’s Not Responsible For Odor Plaguing Murray Hill
summary: Residents in Murray Hill are "appalled" after International Flavors & Fragrances Inc. (IFF) suggested it is not responsible for the foul odors plaguing the neighborhood, despite resident experiences and health impacts. IFF presented findings from a consultant that indicated the odor source might be closer to residential areas, not their facility, a claim many residents dispute. The city councilwoman Randy DeFoor is committed to continuing the investigation to find a solution to the persistent smell.

title: iShares Launches International Small Cap Value ETF, 'ISVL'
summary: BlackRock's iShares has launched a new ETF, the iShares International Developed Small Cap Value Factor ETF (ISVL), to cater to growing investor interest in international small-cap value exposure. This launch follows the recent success of their U.S. counterpart, SVAL, and aims to capitalize on the rally in value stocks since late 2020. ISVL offers a transparent and cost-efficient way for investors to access historically rewarded value and size factors in international markets.

The company, founded in 2013, specializes in manufacturing air filters to custom sizes and specifications. This move will bring new manufacturing operations to the region.

summary: Aramark is implementing various contactless solutions, including self-ordering kiosks, self-checkout scanners, and checkout-free shopping, to enhance the gameday dining experience and ensure safety in sports venues. These services are being rolled out for MLB Opening Day and beyond, supported by Aramark's EverSafe platform which incorporates CDC and WHO recommendations. The company aims to provide a safe, efficient, and frictionless experience for fans returning to stadiums and arenas.

title: AeroVironment Awarded $21 Million Contract Option for Raven Radio Frequency Modifications Under Existing U.S. Army FCS Contract
summary: AeroVironment (NASDAQ: AVAV) announced a $21 million contract option from the U.S. Army for Raven radio frequency modifications. This is the second of three options under an existing multi-year small UAS contract, bringing the total value to date to over $42 million. The contract focuses on upgrading avionics and data links for the Army's Raven tactical UAS fleet, enhancing their mission effectiveness and situational awareness.

title: Acuity Brands Changes Agents in North Jersey
summary: Acuity Brands is changing its sales representation in North Jersey, moving from Liberty Lighting Group to Illuminations Inc. (I2), effective May 1, 2021. This move consolidates the sales coverage for the New York City and Philadelphia metro areas under I2, aiming to provide a single point of contact for customers in these regions. Illuminations Inc. had previously acquired Acuity's sales force in New York City and is now expanding its presence to include North Jersey.

title: Spotlight: Mobile LiDAR delivers unprecedented insights at BHP’s Olympic Dam mine
summary: BHP's Olympic Dam mine has significantly improved its underground operational workflows by adopting Emesent's Hovermap mobile LiDAR system since February 2019. This technology provides accurate, high-resolution data for geotech, engineering, geology, and survey teams, replacing conventional monitoring systems and enhancing understanding of rock mass characteristics and stope management. The system is now integrated into daily operational scheduling, allowing for frequent scanning and data collection without exposing personnel to hazards.

title: Baidu AI Chip Unit Valued at $2 Billion After Raising Fresh Cash
summary: Baidu's AI chip unit, Kunlun, has secured a funding round valuing the company at approximately $2 billion. This first standalone investment round for Kunlun could pave the way for it to expand its client base beyond Baidu and potentially spin off as a separate entity. The move comes as China pushes for tech self-sufficiency, with Baidu planning to invest half of its recent Hong Kong IPO proceeds into AI R&D, including smart driving and AI chips.

It expands Penumbra's portfolio of stroke management solutions, aiming to improve patient outcomes and potentially reduce healthcare costs.

title: Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, Unilever Are Developing 'False' Solutions To Plastic Pollution, Reveals Report
summary: A report by the non-profit Break Free From Plastic movement reveals that major FMCG companies like Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, and Unilever are largely investing in "false solutions" to plastic pollution. Out of 265 corporate projects analyzed from 2018 to April 2021, only 15% focused on proven methods like reuse, refill, and alternative delivery systems, with the vast majority being ineffective or even damaging. Environmental advocates urge these companies to end their reliance on single-use plastics and scale up genuine reuse-based systems instead of promoting misleading initiatives.

summary: Brazilian federal prosecutors have launched an investigation into a $320 million contract with India's Bharat Biotech for 20 million doses of its COVID-19 vaccine. The probe was initiated due to red flags including the high price of the vaccine, the speed of negotiations, and pending regulatory approvals. The contract is also under scrutiny by a Brazilian Senate inquiry, which noted "abnormal pressures" from senior health ministry officials to finalize the deal.

title: Kiewit Said to Withdraw From $2B Newark, NJ AirTrain Competition
summary: Kiewit Corp. has reportedly withdrawn from the competition for the $2-billion AirTrain monorail replacement project at Newark Liberty International Airport. This withdrawal comes amid ongoing federal court litigation between a Kiewit-led team and the Port Authority of New York & New Jersey over disputed costs on the $1.5-billion Goethals Bridge replacement project, where Kiewit claims $100 million. The dispute highlights challenges in design-build contracts, with the Port Authority arguing Kiewit failed to comply with notification requirements for delays and additional costs.

title: ABG-PVH Deal is Latest in Brand Reshuffling
summary: Authentic Brands Group's (ABG) proposed $220 million purchase of PVH Corp.’s Heritage Division (Izod, Van Heusen, Geoffrey Beane, and Arrow) is the latest in a series of brand reshuffling deals among fashion and lifestyle companies. This acquisition highlights a trend where brand management agencies are consolidating retail and fashion brands, intensified by the pandemic-induced downturn in apparel sales. summary: PVH Corp has entered into a definitive agreement to sell the brand trademarks of its Heritage Brands business, including Van Heusen, Arrow, Izod, and Geoffrey Beene, to Authentic Brands Group (ABG) for $220 million. title: Team Ruger’s Maggie Reese Voigt on GetZone.com
summary: Team Ruger’s Maggie Reese Voigt hosts "Ruger American New Shooter Academy: Maggie’s Mission" on GetZone.com, ROKU, and Media Lodge Firearms Platform, teaching firearms safety and use to new shooters. She also provides quick range tips in "Maggie’s Minutes." This initiative, a partnership between Ruger and Media Lodge, aims to educate and welcome new individuals into the shooting community.

title: Raymond James to allow employed advisers to leave and poach clients
summary: Raymond James has introduced a new "employee affiliation model" in the UK, allowing employed advisers to leave the company and take their clients with them, a practice already common in its US and Canadian operations. This model aims to attract entrepreneurial advisers who want to build their own businesses without the full commitment of ownership, offering them training, investment research, and back-office support while maintaining client ownership and control. The company expects this approach to foster growth in its UK market and minimize legal disputes over client ownership, as evidenced by its success in North America.

title: Ralph Lauren partners with G2 Esports
summary: Ralph Lauren has announced a partnership with G2 Esports, naming the fashion company as G2's exclusive fashion outfitter. This collaboration aims to engage new, digitally native consumers through various campaigns and digital-first activations on platforms like TikTok and Twitch. The partnership will also include the Ralph Lauren Wimbledon campaign, featuring League of Legends star Martin 'Rekkles' Larsson.

title: How to succeed in a CIO transition
summary: Former Rollins CIO Lee W. Crump emphasized the advantages of internal succession planning, detailing how a decade-long mentorship program prepared his successor, Thomas Tesh, for the CIO role. This approach minimized disruption, leveraged existing business knowledge, and fostered a smooth transition, highlighting the importance of leadership development within an organization. Crump's experience suggests that growing internal talent is a win-win for both the retiring CIO and the ongoing success of the company.

title: Travel growth: Airline-software company Sabre sees more sales
summary: Sabre, a Southlake-based airline-software company, is experiencing increased sales due to the resurgence of leisure travel. This growth signifies a positive trend for the company as the travel industry recovers.

title: Stantec-designed Anishnawbe Health Centre breaks ground in Toronto
summary: The Anishnawbe Health Centre, designed by Stantec and Two Row Architect, recently broke ground in Toronto's Indigenous Hub. This new four-story, 4181-m² facility will centralize and improve healthcare access for Indigenous communities in Toronto, combining Indigenous and Western approaches with social and cultural programs. The design incorporates Indigenous culture through elements like a perforated metal façade inspired by woven shawls, a central red staircase symbolizing "the red road," and a landscaped courtyard with native plants representing the seven grandfather teachings.

title: High West Rendezvous Rye (2021 Release) Review
summary: This article reviews the 2021 release of High West Rendezvous Rye, which has transitioned from a year-round offering to an annual limited edition with new artwork. The blend, featuring a higher proportion of High West's own distillate, now emphasizes herbal and botanical notes, a departure from its older, spicier iterations. While unique, the review concludes that it lacks the depth of previous releases and struggles to justify its $70 price point, though it remains an interesting whiskey.

LLOG is the operator with a 27.25% working interest, and this is the first of four tieback projects expected online within the next year.

title: Carpet brand Interface aims to run its business "in a way that reverses global warming"
summary: Carpet-tile manufacturer Interface aims to achieve negative carbon emissions by 2040, aligning with its "Climate Take Back" mission to reverse global warming. The company, founded by environmentalist Ray Anderson, has already achieved its "Mission Zero" of zero negative impact by 2020 and now seeks to become carbon negative across its entire value chain. Interface uses recycled and biobased materials, renewable electricity, and offsets for unavoidable emissions, while also launching carbon-negative carpet products like Embodied Beauty and Flash Line, which are negative from "cradle to gate."

summary: Brian Fox, co-founder of Nashville-based Confirmation.com, is departing from his executive role at Thomson Reuters, two years after his company was acquired by the data giant for nearly $500 million. Confirmation.com's sale in 2019, which netted investors $430 million, was one of the largest exits for a local tech company. Fox's departure comes after a significant period following the acquisition.

title: SingleStore updates unified database platform
summary: SingleStore, formerly MemSQL, has released a major update to its unified database platform. This update introduces new storage options, including cloud object storage, and performance improvements such as multicolumn key support. These enhancements are aimed at enabling faster data queries for both transactional and analytical workloads, as highlighted by a case study from IEX Cloud.

title: Zooming in on Hispanic-Serving Institutions—and New HSI Partners Ready to Close the Tech Gap with Netflix
summary: This article discusses the underrepresentation of the Latina/o/x community in key areas like education and tech, highlighting how new partnerships between 2U, Netflix, and Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs) like Marymount University and St. Edward’s University, aim to bridge this gap. It explains the importance and growth of HSIs, which primarily serve Latina/o/x students, and how collaborative programs such as the Netflix Pathways Boot Camps offer essential tech skills and professional development to create pathways into technology careers. The piece emphasizes the critical role of HSIs in educating an underserved population and the power of public-private partnerships in fostering economic development and diversity in the workforce.

Valmont Coatings received honors in the Industrial, Artistic, Duplex Systems, and International categories for various projects across North America and India.

title: Vodafone’s European network 100% powered from renewables
summary: Vodafone announced that its entire European operations, including networks, data centers, retail, and offices, will be 100% powered by renewable electricity from July 1, 2021. This move is a significant step towards the company's goal of achieving 'net zero' carbon emissions by 2030 and across its value chain by 2040. Vodafone also aims to help its business customers reduce their carbon emissions by a cumulative 350 million tonnes over ten years and is committed to reducing waste and promoting a circular economy.

summary: Harvey Breaux, a part sales coordinator based in New Iberia, celebrates 30 years with Bristow Group. Breaux values the relationships built over the years and offers advice to new employees, emphasizing the importance of perspective.

title: WD is fixing a bug that makes Black SN850 SSDs run slow on X570 motherboards
summary: Western Digital has identified a bug causing their Black SN850 SSDs to experience a significant drop in write performance when connected to the chipset M.2 slot on certain AMD X570 motherboards. The company plans to release a firmware update by mid-July 2021 to address this issue. Until the fix is available, a workaround involves connecting the SSD to a CPU-controlled M.2 slot where performance is unaffected.

summary: Boral Limited has agreed to sell its North American Building Products business to a subsidiary of Westlake Chemical Corporation for $2.15 billion. The sale includes operations in roofing, stone, light building products, and windows, with Boral’s North American building products generating over $1 billion in revenue in 2020. This transaction is expected to expand Westlake's housing-related building products business and is anticipated to be completed in the first half of fiscal year 2022.

title: Self-driving startup WeRide deepens ties with Nissan, raises $310 million
summary: WeRide, a China-based autonomous driving startup, announced a deeper collaboration with Nissan on self-driving technology for the Chinese market. The company also raised $310 million in funding, bringing its valuation to $3.3 billion. WeRide aims to achieve Level 4 autonomous driving standards and is currently testing vehicles in multiple locations, including California and Chinese cities.

title: Brendan Hoffman Set to Become Wolverine CEO
summary: Brendan Hoffman, currently the president of Wolverine Worldwide, is slated to become the company's new CEO at the end of the year, succeeding Blake Krueger. Hoffman's diverse background in retail, wholesale, and digital will be crucial as Wolverine transitions from a wholesale-heavy model to one with a stronger direct-to-consumer focus. The company plans to invest in people, AI, IT systems, and potential acquisitions to react quickly to consumer trends and expand its global base and offerings into new categories like apparel.

title: Yelp announces the Top Backyard Trends of Summer 2021 with famed interior designer Jeremiah Brent
summary: Yelp, in collaboration with interior designer Jeremiah Brent, has identified the top backyard trends for Summer 2021, driven by increased interest in outdoor spaces. The trends include elevated al fresco entertaining, creating outdoor living rooms, deck and patio additions, water features, easy rustic landscaping, backyard oases, and reducing and reusing. These insights are based on Yelp's data science team analyzing search and review mentions, with Brent offering expert tips for each trend.

title: El Gobierno autorizó la compra de Edenor: sale Mindlin, entran Vila y Manzano
summary: The Argentine government has officially authorized the sale of Edenor, the country's largest electricity distributor, from Marcelo Mindlin's Pampa Energía to a group led by Daniel Vila and José Luis Manzano for $95 million. This transaction marks a significant shift in the energy sector, transferring control from an entrepreneur favored by the previous Macri government to a group with close ties to the current administration. title: Exxon must face Massachusetts lawsuit alleging climate change deceit
summary: A Massachusetts state judge has ruled that Exxon Mobil Corp must face a lawsuit brought by Attorney General Maura Healey, which alleges the oil company misled consumers and investors about its role in climate change. The judge rejected Exxon's attempt to dismiss the case, stating that many of Exxon's statements referenced in the complaint are not protected. This decision follows an activist hedge fund winning board seats at Exxon, intensifying pressure on the energy giant regarding global warming concerns.

title: Focus: Boeing faces rocky path to gaining approval for 737 MAX return in China
summary: Boeing is facing significant delays in getting its 737 MAX aircraft approved for return to service in China due to political tensions, regulatory hurdles, and China's ambition to boost its homegrown aerospace industry. Despite the MAX being approved in other parts of the world, China's Civil Aviation Administration has not yet given clearance, impacting Boeing's production plans and market share. This situation is further complicated by the ongoing geopolitical climate and China's conservative approach to aviation safety.

title: YouTuber Takes 600-HP Smart Car To CarMax, Gets Humorous Offer
summary: YouTuber FasterProms took his highly modified, 600-horsepower turbo Smart Car to CarMax for an appraisal, despite having invested thousands into its conversion with a Honda K-series engine. Due to its extreme modifications, lack of essential components like doors and an odometer, and general impracticality, CarMax offered a mere $500 for the vehicle. The YouTuber ultimately decided to keep the car, recognizing its higher value to him for content creation rather than its paltry resale value.

summary: Wattpad and Webtoon are merging to create Wattpad WEBTOON Studios, a new entertainment studio focused on adapting stories from both platforms into movies and TV series. The studio, owned by South Korean media company Naver, will develop comic and YA properties and already has over 100 projects in development or production. summary: The FDA has granted accelerated approval to Seagen and Genmab's drug Tivdak for cervical cancer patients whose tumors have relapsed or spread after chemotherapy. summary: GreenLight Biosciences is establishing a new $16.6 million manufacturing plant in Rochester at Eastman Business Park to produce enzymes and RNA for agricultural applications, including bee protection. This 17,000-square-foot facility will leverage GreenLight's clean, cell-free RNA production process to create targeted biocontrols for pests. The company plans to create up to 30 new jobs and has ambitions to address human health needs, including developing mRNA vaccines for influenza and COVID-19.

title: FedEx Cuts Forecast, Blaming Labor Shortages for Rising Costs
summary: FedEx (FDX) has cut its annual profit outlook after missing quarterly earnings estimates due to higher costs and stagnant shipment growth. The company attributes these issues primarily to a tight labor market, which has driven up wages, reduced network efficiencies, and increased reliance on external transportation services, resulting in an estimated $450 million in added costs. Following the announcement, FedEx shares declined by as much as 5% in after-hours trading.

summary: This review praises Netflix and Hasbro's "My Little Pony: New Generations" as a great tribute to previous MLP incarnations, offering throwbacks to the 80s version and lore from "Friendship is Magic." The film is commended for its easy-to-understand approach to social issues like prejudice and fear for children, and its innovative animation and character design. title: HexAM by Hexcel awarded long-term contract for Boeing 777X AM parts
summary: Hexcel Corporation secured a multi-year contract to produce aerospace structures using its HexAM additive manufacturing process for the Boeing 777X aircraft. These parts, made with HexPEKK-100 material, are crucial for commercial aerospace, defense, and space applications due to their complexity, lightweight, and strong mechanical performance, meeting interior aircraft smoke and toxicity requirements. These findings could support broader booster availability and increase the vaccine's usage.

title: Justice Department requires Polly-O and Athenos divestitures after Kraft Heinz-Lactalis deal
summary: The Justice Department has mandated the divestiture of the Polly-O and Athenos brands as a condition for the Kraft Heinz-Lactalis deal to proceed. These transactions, with Polly-O going to BelGioioso Cheese and Athenos to Emmi Roth, were already in progress and are expected to settle the antitrust matter. This requirement stems from an antitrust review following Kraft Heinz's sale of its natural cheese business to Lactalis for $3.2 billion.

title: Kilroy Pays $490M for Amazon-Anchored Tower
summary: Kilroy Realty Corp. acquired West 8th, a 539,000-square-foot, LEED Platinum certified office tower in Seattle, for $490 million. The building is fully leased, with Amazon occupying approximately 70 percent of the space, and was previously purchased by DWS Group in 2016 for $370 million. This acquisition expands Kilroy's Seattle footprint and follows other significant investments and a disposition by the REIT in Texas and San Francisco.

Haddad plans to advocate for public-private partnerships in housing and education, and develop nonresidential projects with a focus on health care and entertainment.

title: Rewalk Robotics (RWLK) Stock Price Rallied 42.3% as Retail Investors Pushed It Higher
summary: Rewalk Robotics (RWLK) stock rallied 42.3% due to significant buying pressure from retail investors, despite no recent major announcements. The surge, which some traders consider a short squeeze, saw the stock price increase from $1.30 to $1.85, driven by a large volume of shares traded. The company's low stock price makes it an attractive target for retail investors.

title: Access to College Just Got Easier: Stride Taps into Acadeum’s Dual Enrollment Consortium
summary: K12 Private Academy, a private school for grades K–12, and Acadeum, a company helping colleges and universities share courses, have partnered to provide high school students with access to over 500 online college-level courses through a new dual enrollment program. This initiative aims to address the student debt crisis and disparities in dual enrollment access by making online college courses more universally available to eligible high school students, allowing them to earn college credits and explore associate degree pathways.

title: New Sustainable Happy Meal Toys
summary: McDonald's announced its ambition to drastically reduce plastics and offer sustainable Happy Meal toys globally by the end of 2025, aiming for an approximately 90% reduction in virgin fossil fuel-based plastic use compared to 2018. This initiative involves transitioning to more renewable, recycled, and certified materials, with existing efforts already resulting in a 30% reduction since 2018. The company is collaborating with scientists, toy makers, and suppliers, and drawing inspiration from children and families to ensure the fun factor remains high while making a positive environmental impact.

title: McDonald’s sets new goals for sustainable Happy Meal toys
summary: McDonald's has announced new global sustainability goals to reduce virgin fossil-fuel plastics in its Happy Meal toys by 90% within the next five years, aiming for completion by the end of 2025. The company plans to transition to more renewable, recycled, and certified materials, driven by customer feedback concerning environmental worries. This initiative has already begun in some international markets, with plans to introduce paper-based or plant-derived toys globally.

title: Platinum Equity Announces Sale Of Singapore-Based Electronics Manufacturing Services Provider PCI To Celestica
summary: Platinum Equity announced the signing of a definitive agreement to sell PCI Limited, a Singapore-based electronics manufacturing services provider, to Celestica Inc. for $306 million in cash. The sale is expected to close in mid-fourth quarter of 2021, subject to regulatory approval and customary closing conditions. Platinum Equity had acquired PCI in April 2019 and significantly grew its revenue and profitability through strategic investments and operational improvements.

A judge denied Willis's request for a temporary restraining order and expedited discovery, while Marsh has sought to dismiss the case.

title: Bruno Mars Performed at Swanky Cape Cod Wedding Last Weekend
summary: Bruno Mars performed a private concert at a lavish, seven-figure wedding on Cape Cod for the son of Motorola Solutions, Inc. CEO Greg Brown. The singer reportedly received upwards of $3 million for his appearance, drawing crowds of curious residents to catch a glimpse or hear his performance outside the Chatham Bars Inn. Wedding guests were required to show proof of vaccination or a negative COVID test to attend the event at the upscale venue.

title: Materialise releases Magics module for automated AM preparation in dental labs
summary: Materialise NV has launched a new Dental Module for its Magics software, designed to optimize and automate Additive Manufacturing preparation workflows for dental labs. This module streamlines the process of preparing 3D files for common dental applications like crowns and bridges, reducing manual effort and allowing specialists to focus on other patient responsibilities. A free webinar providing further details on the Dental Module is scheduled for October 14, 2021.

title: U.S. Bank to Buy MUFG Union Bank for $8B
summary: U.S. Bancorp announced an agreement to acquire MUFG Union Bank for approximately $8 billion, comprising $5.5 billion in cash and $2.5 billion in stock. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2022 and aims for significant cost synergies while preserving front-line branch employees.

summary: S&P Global announced its status as a founding member of the newly launched Net Zero Financial Services Provider Alliance (NZFSPA), which aims to align financial services with achieving a net zero economy by 2050. This alliance, part of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), will help mobilize capital towards a net zero transition by providing essential data and products to financial institutions. title: Sempra Foundation And GRID Alternatives Announce Contribution To Solar Projects Intended To Improve Energy Access In Mexico
summary: Sempra Foundation and GRID Alternatives have partnered to contribute over $200,000 to solar projects in Mexico, aiming to improve energy access for vulnerable communities. These projects include grid-tied solar installations for community buildings and off-grid solutions for families, focusing on areas with environmental justice concerns. The initiative also includes training for local students in clean energy careers and is expected to avoid significant greenhouse gas emissions.

summary: PayPal has launched a new all-in-one app designed to be a central hub for customers' financial lives, introducing high-yield savings accounts provided by Synchrony Bank, in-app shopping tools with rewards, and early access Direct Deposit. This updated app aims to simplify digital payments and financial management, offering features like bill pay, crypto services, and personalized dashboards. summary: Chih Lin and Mike Dorsey transitioned from unfulfilling corporate jobs to create Dumpling Dudez, a business centered around Lin's family dumpling-making legacy. summary: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) has announced it will sell its core banking subsidiary, MUFG Union Bank (MUB), to U.S Bancorp (USB) in an US$8 billion deal expected to close in Q1 2022. summary: U.S. Bank is acquiring MUFG Union Bank in an approximately $8 billion cash-and-stock deal, expected to close in the first half of 2022. title: Ventas Completes Acquisition of New Senior Investment Group Inc.
summary: Ventas, Inc. has completed its acquisition of New Senior Investment Group Inc. in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $2.3 billion. This acquisition is expected to position Ventas to capitalize on the senior housing market's growth, adding a high-quality independent living portfolio and building on existing relationships. Shares of New Senior common stock will no longer be traded on the New York Stock Exchange.

title: Westrock Coffee Company Announces They Will Be 100% Responsibly Sourced by 2025
summary: Westrock Coffee Company announced its commitment to sourcing 100% of its coffee and tea responsibly by 2025, building on a sustainability journey that began 12 years ago. To achieve this, the company will implement a global supplier assurance framework in partnership with COSA and BSI, and deploy personnel to quantify the impact of their supply chains. This initiative underscores Westrock Coffee's dedication to ethical practices, transparency, and supporting sustainable growth for farmers.

title: Inside Wells Fargo’s multicloud strategy
summary: Wells Fargo is implementing a decade-long multicloud strategy, partnering with Microsoft and Google to modernize its technology infrastructure for public cloud operations. This approach, while different from some competitors, aims for portability, resilience, and avoids vendor lock-in, addressing the challenges of migrating highly regulated data and upskilling its workforce. The financial institution plans to progressively move existing applications to the public cloud, prioritizing impact over speed, with the ultimate goal of moving away from traditional data centers.

title: Universal Music Shares Soar in Market Debut
summary: Shares of Universal Music Group NV, the world's largest music company, surged by 36% in their market debut on the Euronext exchange in Amsterdam. This strong performance signals investor confidence in the resurgent music industry. The company was spun off from French media conglomerate Vivendi SE.

title: Canada's Aurora Cannabis to shut down a facility in Edmonton
summary: Aurora Cannabis Inc. announced on Tuesday its decision to close a facility in Edmonton, Alberta, facing ongoing financial difficulties exacerbated by the pandemic. Medical distribution will be relocated to the Aurora Sky factory, and manufacturing will be moved to the Aurora River factory in Ontario. This move aligns with the company's strategy to become a "leaner, more agile organization" and follows previous staff reductions and facility closures in June of the prior year.

title: Entergy Corporation Proposes Potential Pathways Forward for Entergy New Orleans
summary: Entergy Corporation has proposed four preliminary options for the future operation and ownership of its subsidiary, Entergy New Orleans, LLC, in response to a New Orleans City Council proposal to study municipalization. These options include a merger with Entergy Louisiana, a sale to another entity, establishing Entergy New Orleans as a standalone company, or municipalization by the City of New Orleans. The company is prepared to support the City Council in evaluating these pathways, emphasizing its long history and contributions to the city.

title: FedEx labor shortfall hits quarterly profit, earnings forecast
summary: FedEx (FDX.N) reported a 7% drop in quarterly profit and lowered its full-year earnings forecast due to labor shortages, which led to increased costs and slowed package delivery. The company incurred an extra $450 million in costs from higher wages, overtime, and third-party transportation, particularly affecting its Ground network which is now rerouting 600,000 packages daily. FedEx plans to hire 90,000 holiday workers to address staffing issues as it prepares for the peak season.

title: McDonald's Happy Meal toys to go green globally by 2025
summary: McDonald's announced that it will drastically reduce plastic use in its Happy Meal toys globally by the end of 2025, aiming for a 90% cut in virgin fossil fuel-based plastic compared to 2018. This change involves swapping plastic figurines for toys made from recycled, plant-based plastics, or cardboard. The company has already implemented similar initiatives in some markets and plans to expand these efforts worldwide.

title: Apparel giant with large Triad presence snaps up N.C company in $168M acquisition
summary: Gildan Activewear has acquired Frontier Yarns of Sanford for $168 million. Frontier Yarns operates four facilities in North Carolina, including two in the Triad, and employs approximately 800 people. This acquisition will expand Gildan's distribution center in Eden.

title: General Mills names Doug Martin new chief brand officer
summary: General Mills has appointed Doug Martin as its new chief brand and disruptive growth officer, effective January 3, 2022. Martin previously served as chief disruptive growth officer at General Mills and led the successful launch of the Oui by Yoplait brand.

title: Goldman Sachs BDC Appoints Chi and Miller as Co-CEOs and Co-Presidents
summary: Goldman Sachs BDC, Inc. announced Alex Chi and David Miller, co-heads of Goldman Sachs Asset Management Private Credit in the Americas, will become co-CEOs and co-Presidents effective March 2022. This transition follows Brendan McGovern's decision to retire after a 15-year career at Goldman Sachs, with him remaining in his role until March to ensure a smooth handover. Julian Salisbury, Global Head of Goldman Sachs Asset Management, noted that Chi and Miller bring over 40 years of combined experience at the firm to their new leadership roles.

title: Gov. Eric Holcomb appoints Cynthia Lucchese to Indiana University Board of Trustees
summary: Indiana Governor Eric Holcomb has appointed Cynthia "Cindy" Lucchese, an innovative business leader and IU alumna, to the Indiana University Board of Trustees. Lucchese, former CFO for Hillenbrand Inc. and Thoratec Corp., and currently chief strategy officer for Penske Entertainment, will fill the vacancy left by the passing of Trustee Melanie S. Walker. Her financial expertise and deep understanding of IU's mission are expected to benefit the board significantly.

summary: Linda Heasley, former J.Jill CEO, has been appointed president and CEO of Janie and Jack by brand investment platform Go Global Retail. summary: Novartis has entered into an option, collaboration, and license agreement with BeiGene for the TIGIT inhibitor ociperlimab, enhancing its immunotherapy pipeline, particularly for oncology. title: U.S. FDA approves expanded use of Amgen's psoriasis drug
summary: The U.S. FDA has approved the expanded use of Amgen Inc.'s drug Otezla to treat adults with mild to moderate plaque psoriasis, making it the first and only oral treatment option for this patient category. Otezla, acquired by Amgen in 2019 for $13.4 billion, generated $2.2 billion in sales last year and is also being tested for other conditions. Plaque psoriasis affects approximately 6.7 million adults in the United States and is the most common form of the skin disease.

summary: Western companies providing essential goods like food and medicine in Russia are caught between balancing the Russian government's demands and calls from Ukraine supporters to fully withdraw. summary: A federal jury ruled that a born-again Christian employee's religious beliefs did not conflict with his employer's mandatory Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) training. summary: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion announced significant changes to how medical collection debt will be reported, aiming to remove nearly 70% of such debt tradelines from consumer credit reports. Effective July 1, paid medical collection debt will no longer be included, and the period before unpaid debt appears on a report will increase from 6 months to one year. Additionally, in the first half of 2023, medical collection debt under $500 will no longer be included on credit reports.

title: Here’s the latest on possible 4th COVID-19 vaccine shot for Americans
summary: Moderna has requested FDA authorization for a fourth COVID-19 vaccine booster for all adults, while Pfizer and BioNTech sought approval for seniors aged 65 and older, citing data from Israel showing reduced infection and severe disease rates. U.S. health officials are considering additional booster doses and seeking funding to secure more vaccines, amidst ongoing studies on omicron-specific and hybrid shots. Experts like Dr. Paul Offit question the necessity of a fourth shot for most people, emphasizing that protection against severe illness should be the primary goal.

title: Inside the Forces Driving Senior Living Valuations in 2022
summary: The article discusses the various forces influencing senior living valuations in 2022, including depressed occupancy, staffing shortages, higher expenses, and compressed margins, which led to a slight dip in average sale prices per unit in 2021. Despite recent challenges, capital providers are showing renewed interest in senior housing assets, particularly Class A properties or those with strong operators, with experts anticipating an increase in per-unit community prices as the market normalizes and occupancy rates rise. The narrowing bid-ask spread and increased competitiveness in lending and equity markets are also expected to drive valuations up, although some companies like HTI are holding off on sales due to anticipated future growth and clearer returns.
