title: Lockheed Martin delivered its 500th C-130J Super Hercules airlifter
summary: Lockheed Martin has delivered its 500th C-130J Super Hercules airlifter, which is a C-130J-30 aircraft assigned to the 130th Airlift Wing in West Virginia. This milestone highlights the C-130J's global presence with 26 operators in 22 nations and marks the U.S. government's continued transition to this common platform across its military branches. The C-130J is acclaimed for its versatility, with 17 different mission configurations, and its fleet has amassed over 2 million flight hours.

title: Laird Superfood appoints Daryl Moore as its new senior vice president
summary: Laird Superfood, Inc. has appointed Daryl Moore as its new Senior Vice President of Sales. Moore brings over 30 years of leadership experience in the food and beverage industry and will focus on national expansion within all wholesale channels. This appointment follows Jason Vieth's role as CEO and President, and Moore expresses enthusiasm for driving growth with Laird Superfood's mission-driven brand.

title: Koch Modular to supply modular recycling system for PureCycle PP facility
summary: Koch Modular Process Systems, LLC is expanding its partnership with PureCycle Technologies, Inc. to supply modular recycling systems for PureCycle's facilities, starting with one in Augusta, Georgia. This multi-year master services agreement aims to address the global need for transforming plastic waste into a renewable resource and reflects PureCycle's confidence in Koch Modular's capabilities. The collaboration builds on a six-year history, including previous work on PureCycle's Ironton facility, to achieve a goal of one billion pounds of like-new, ultra-pure recycled plastic production capacity.

title: SAP and Unilever Pilot Blockchain Technology to Support Deforestation-Free Palm Oil
summary: SAP SE and Unilever announced a pilot program using GreenToken by SAP to enhance traceability and transparency in Unilever’s global palm oil supply chain. The solution aims to track palm oil from sustainable sources through the entire supply chain to ensure a deforestation-free origin. A successful proof of concept in Indonesia tracked over 188,000 tons of oil palm fruit, enabling suppliers to create tokens mirroring material flow and origin attributes.

title: Hong Kong’s immunized who died of COVID mainly got Sinovac vaccine: Ming Pao
summary: A report by Ming Pao newspaper indicates that 87% of vaccinated individuals in Hong Kong who died from COVID-19 received Sinovac Biotech Ltd.'s vaccine, although most COVID-related deaths were among the unvaccinated. The analysis noted that Sinovac was often preferred by the elderly despite lower efficacy against Omicron compared to BioNTech, with a significant proportion of elderly vaccine doses being Sinovac. Experts have recommended BioNTech for better protection for the elderly and children.

title: Moody’s upgrades Assured Guaranty
summary: Moody's Investors Service has upgraded the insurance financial strength (IFS) ratings of Assured Guaranty and its subsidiaries, reflecting improved credit profiles after resolving exposure to Puerto Rico bonds. The upgrades include Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (AGM) and Assured Guaranty UK Limited (AGUK) to A1, and Assured Guaranty Corp. (AGC) to A2, with a stable outlook for all ratings. This positive assessment is also supported by growing demand for financial guaranty insurance and the stabilization and slow growth of AGM's insured portfolio.

title: Pakistan, Foreign Developer Agree to Restart Work on Massive Gold and Copper Mine
summary: Pakistan has settled a long-running dispute with international mining companies Barrick Gold Corp. and Antofagasta, agreeing to restart work on the massive Reko Diq gold and copper mine. The deal waives an $11 billion penalty against Pakistan and involves Barrick investing nearly $10 billion in Balochistan, creating over 8,000 jobs. Pakistan and Barrick Gold will each own 50% of the new project company, with Antofagasta exiting the venture.

summary: Black Spade Asia Acquisition, a SPAC backed by Melco's chairman Lawrence Ho and BOCHK Asset Management, has applied to list on the Hong Kong stock exchange. This marks the 11th SPAC to seek listing in Hong Kong, and the second by a local tycoon within a week. SPACs in Hong Kong must raise at least HK$1 billion and announce a deal within 24 months.

title: Starbucks Hit With Tech Glitches, Disrupting Orders and Frustrating Customers
summary: Starbucks experienced widespread technical glitches this week, affecting mobile ordering and credit-card processing at numerous U.S. cafes. These disruptions led to longer customer wait times and frustration for both customers and baristas. The issues highlight the company's increasing reliance on technology for its dominant to-go business, which accounts for about 75% of U.S. company store sales.

summary: Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine (RUSVM) celebrated its 2022 commencement, graduating over 400 students from various regions who will address a critical shortage in the veterinary workforce. title: Seattle woman found guilty in massive 2019 hack of Capital One data
summary: A federal jury in Seattle convicted former Amazon software engineer Paige Thompson of several charges related to a massive 2019 hack of Capital One bank and other companies. Her sentencing is scheduled for September, with potential penalties including up to 20 years for wire fraud and five years for the other charges.

summary: Latham & Watkins LLP advised Lucid Energy Group in its US$3.55 billion acquisition by Targa Resources Corp. Lucid Energy Group, the largest privately held natural gas processor in the Permian Basin, was acquired from Riverstone Holdings LLC and Goldman Sachs Asset Management. The transaction involved a multidisciplinary team from Latham & Watkins covering corporate, tax, benefits, antitrust, energy regulatory, environmental, data privacy, finance, real estate, insurance, sanctions, RWI, intellectual property, and capital markets matters.

title: Elon Musk and Tesla sued over Dogecoin ‘pyramid scheme’
summary: Elon Musk and Tesla are being sued for $258 billion by a Dogecoin investor who alleges they ran a pyramid scheme to inflate the cryptocurrency's value. The plaintiff, Keith Johnson, claims Musk manipulated Dogecoin for "profit, exposure and amusement" despite knowing it had no intrinsic value, and seeks damages for the $86 billion decline in Dogecoin's market value since May 2021. Johnson also wants to prevent Musk and his companies from promoting Dogecoin and to have it declared gambling under federal and New York law.

title: $6.5B Texas Instruments Fab Could Be First of Four at Site Totaling $30B
summary: Texas Instruments plans to build up to four semiconductor chip fabrication plants in Sherman, Texas, with the first $6.5 billion fab already under construction and expected to begin production in 2025. The total investment for all four plants could reach nearly $30 billion, supported by significant local incentives. This development is part of a broader U.S. push to increase domestic semiconductor manufacturing amidst global shortages.

title: Textron Aviation adds to Denali testing program
summary: Textron Aviation has expanded its Beechcraft Denali flight test program by adding a second test aircraft. The new turboprop is manufactured in east Wichita. This advancement marks a significant step in the Denali program's development.

title: Dividend Hikes Are Happening Despite Recession Fears
summary: Despite inflation fears, rate hikes, and recession concerns, many companies are increasing their dividends, signaling confidence in their businesses. While individual stock picking can be challenging, dividend-focused ETFs like the Vanguard High Dividend Yield Index Fund ETF Shares (VYM) offer a convenient way for investors to access companies with high dividend yields. This strategy allows investors to find good buying opportunities in a volatile market by focusing on defensive stocks that can withstand inflation.

title: Walmart Is Pulling MyPillow Products From Shelves
summary: Walmart is no longer carrying MyPillow products in its stores, though they remain available online. This decision comes as MyPillow's CEO, Mike Lindell, faces litigation related to his unproven claims of fraud in the 2020 election. Lindell stated that Walmart cited his products not meeting internal rating criteria as the reason for their removal from shelves.

title: GroupM Nexus Enhances Its Media Transformation Through New Leadership Appointments
summary: GroupM Nexus, WPP’s performance media investment group, has announced new leadership appointments following its recent media agency mergers. These appointments follow the consolidation of GroupM Nexus, EssenceMediaCom, and Mindshare with Neo, aimed at powering growth for its people, agencies, and brands. The new leadership team includes global CEOs, COOs, and chief officers across various functions, with further changes expected in the coming months.

title: Starbucks Executive Exits After Sparring With Union Organizers
summary: Starbucks' North America president, Rossann Williams, is stepping down after more than four years in the role, to be replaced by Sara Trilling. Williams' departure comes amid increased unionization efforts within the company, with which she had reportedly sparred. Trilling, a 20-year Starbucks veteran, will take over at the end of the month.

title: TikTok moves U.S. user data to Oracle servers
summary: TikTok has completed the migration of its U.S. user data to servers at Oracle Corp, aiming to address U.S. regulatory concerns regarding data integrity. This move comes after a U.S. national security panel previously ordered ByteDance to divest TikTok due to fears that user data could be accessed by China's government. TikTok will now delete private U.S. user data from its own data centers and rely fully on Oracle's U.S. servers, also establishing a dedicated U.S. data security team, "USDS," to ringfence this information from ByteDance.

title: These former Comcast guys are looking to personalize online sports betting
summary: Former Comcast executives Chris Reynolds and Jason Angelides have launched a Philadelphia tech startup called Epoxy.ai, aiming to personalize the online sports betting experience. Their technology will sync TV viewing with recommended bets, initially using a mobile phone microphone to identify the game being watched. BetParx is their first customer, with plans to launch the Epoxy app for the NFL season despite some industry reservations about the current focus on core innovation versus personalization in the still-developing online betting market.

title: CSX plans on demolishing 95-year-old roundhouse on Far South Side. Some want to save it.
summary: CSX Transportation intends to demolish a 95-year-old brick roundhouse on Columbus's Far South Side, despite efforts by preservation groups like the Columbus Landmarks Foundation to save it. The foundation and other advocates argue for the historic building's adaptive reuse, suggesting it could become a community gathering place or a farmers' market, similar to other redeveloped historic structures in the area. CSX states the demolition is part of a systemwide infrastructure maintenance and cleanup program, prioritizing a safe work environment, but has not set a timeline for when the demolition would begin.

title: CFPB to revisit QM rule, New Residential renames itself, Wells Fargo disputes suits and more of the week's top news
summary: This article summarizes the top mortgage industry news from the week of June 18, 2022. Key topics include the CFPB's plan to review the Qualified Mortgage rule, New Residential Investment Corp. rebranding to Rithm Capital, and Wells Fargo disputing discrimination lawsuits. Other significant events covered are surging mortgage rates, increased foreclosures, a data breach at Lower, and new loan offerings from First Guaranty Bank.

title: Colonel Tom Parker angled to bring Celine Dion to Las Vegas
summary: The article details how Elvis Presley's former manager, Colonel Tom Parker, attempted to bring Celine Dion to Las Vegas years before her successful residency at The Colosseum. Parker recognized Dion's talent after hearing her cover "Can't Help Falling in Love" and repeatedly advocated for her to perform on the Strip, trying to place her at the Hilton and later The Mirage. Despite his efforts, Dion's manager at the time felt she wasn't ready for American audiences, and Steve Wynn already had Siegfried & Roy booked.

title: How the massive EV transition is starting in the car rental industry
summary: The car rental industry is undergoing a significant transition to electric vehicles (EVs), led by Hertz's substantial purchase of Teslas, followed by moves from Enterprise and Avis. This shift, however, faces challenges such as limited EV availability, insufficient charging infrastructure, and the need to educate both employees and customers. Despite these hurdles, rental companies are targeting corporate clients who seek to meet ESG goals through EV adoption, and the industry is seen as crucial for broader public exposure to EVs.

title: Class-action suit charges Ralph Lauren sweater swindle
summary: A class-action lawsuit claims Ralph Lauren Corp. misled customers about the material content of its sweaters. Texas resident Gloria Miramontes purchased a V-neck sweater advertised as 100% Pima cotton, a high-end fiber, but lab tests allegedly proved it was not. The suit, seeking $5 million, covers customers from 19 states who were sold sweaters that were not entirely Pima cotton.

title: The Gateway At Wynwood Leases 14,000 Square Feet Across Three New-To-Market Tenants
summary: The Gateway at Wynwood, a 12-story boutique office building in Miami, has secured three new tenants, occupying nearly 14,000 square feet. The new occupants include Spearmint Energy, Victory Polymers Corps., and Ripple, marking their first offices in South Florida. These leases highlight the increasing appeal of The Gateway at Wynwood for new-to-market companies.

title: Former Amazon employee convicted in Capital One hack
summary: A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of hacking into Capital One and stealing the data of over 100 million people, making it one of the largest data breaches in the U.S. Thompson was found guilty of seven federal crimes, including wire fraud, and her sentencing is set for September 15. Capital One has previously agreed to pay $190 million to settle a class-action lawsuit and an additional $80 million in regulatory fines related to the breach.

title: MLA doubtful Taltson project will help N.W.T. achieve its climate goals
summary: Yellowknife North MLA Rylund Johnson expresses doubt that the Taltson hydro expansion project will be completed by 2030, making it unlikely for the N.W.T. to meet its greenhouse gas emission reduction targets. The project relies on connecting to new mines that are not guaranteed to open or commit to purchasing power, and the existing diamond mines are projected to close before the expansion is operational. Although federal support for feasibility studies exists, significant funding gaps and a lack of alternative plans from the territory raise concerns about achieving climate goals.

title: Business Matters: Great Lakes Bay Construction has 55 employees, serves customers in 5 states
summary: Great Lakes Bay Construction, owned by Shawn Pnacek and his uncle Patrick Pnacek, has been in business for 10 years, employing 55 people and serving customers in five states from its Midland headquarters. The company specializes in design-build and general contracting for commercial and industrial markets and is actively involved in the local community through various initiatives. Shawn Pnacek highlights Midland's talent pool, central location, and strong community support as key factors in the company's success and choice to remain based there.

title: Globalstar hush-hush ahead of launch with SpaceX
summary: Globalstar is preparing to launch its FM15 spare satellite on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral, expected early Sunday. Despite SpaceX announcing and planning to webcast the launch, Globalstar has remained largely silent, only mentioning the spare satellite in a financial report. This mission marks the first Globalstar satellite launch since 2013, adding capacity to its commercial data relay network, with the company also planning to launch 17 new satellites by late 2025.

title: Garmin Venu 2 Plus review: Packed with fitness and smart features
summary: The Garmin Venu 2 Plus is a premium fitness smartwatch that offers a blend of style, comprehensive fitness tracking, and useful smart features like the ability to make and take calls. While it comes with a high price tag and some minor software usability quirks, its accurate tracking, long battery life, and elegant design make it a strong contender for those serious about fitness who want an alternative to Apple Watch or Samsung Galaxy Watch.

title: Review : Hotel Marriott Calgary Airport Terminal | Marriott Bonvoy
summary: This article reviews the Marriott Calgary Airport Terminal Hotel, highlighting its convenient location directly within the airport, especially for late arrivals or early departures. The review details the experience from checking in and getting a suite upgrade to the amenities offered, including the spacious room, M Club Lounge, YAKIMA Social Kitchen + Bar, OraOxygen Spa, and fitness center. The author recommends the hotel for families and business travelers and would return for future stays in Calgary.

title: Todd Gilliland delivers early Father’s Day present with Knoxville win
summary: Todd Gilliland secured an emotional win in the NASCAR Camping World Truck Series Clean Harbors 150 at Knoxville Raceway, marking his first start of the season and third career victory. The win, coming just before Father's Day, was dedicated to his father and team owner, David Gilliland. The race also saw Carson Hocevar's dominant run end prematurely due to an engine failure, opening the door for Gilliland to take the lead and hold off John Hunter Nemechek.

title: Cardi B Helping Playboy Rake in Huge Returns
summary: Cardi B's role as Playboy Magazine's Creative Director in Residence and Founding Creative Director of CENTERFOLD has significantly boosted the company's financial performance. Playboy's parent company, PLBY, reported a 63% growth and a 125% increase in direct-to-consumer revenue since she took on the positions. Her work focuses on empowering content creators and expanding the brand's digital presence and merchandise.

title: Rogers to sell Freedom Mobile to Quebecor Inc. for $2.85B
summary: Rogers Communications Inc. has agreed to sell Freedom Mobile to Quebecor Inc. for $2.85 billion in an effort to satisfy federal regulators' competition concerns regarding its proposed $26-billion acquisition of Shaw Communications. This deal, which includes Freedom's customers, infrastructure, and spectrum, aims to maintain a competitive wireless market in Canada. However, Globalive Capital, a competing bidder, criticized the sale, claiming Rogers chose Quebecor to avoid a stronger long-term competitor.

title: Stryker receives FDA clearance for spine surgery planning, navigation platform
summary: Stryker has secured FDA 510(k) clearance for its Q guidance system, an advanced platform for planning and intraoperative guidance in spine surgery. The system integrates multiple tracking options, software algorithms, smart instrumentation, and a high-performance navigation camera to provide a comprehensive procedural ecosystem. This clearance is a step towards streamlining technologies across various medical specialties, with plans for future integration of robotics and intelligent handheld instruments.

title: “Estación Saturno”, el paraje ferroviaro abandonado que recibirá todo el gas del Gasoducto Néstor Kirchner
summary: The article discusses "Estación Saturno," an abandoned railway area in the municipality of Guaminí, Argentina, which will become a key reception point for gas from the Néstor Kirchner Gas Pipeline. Although Salliqueló is publicly named, the gas pipeline will physically terminate in Saturno, where a significant compressor plant built in 1994 is located. This development is expected to reactivate the area, bringing economic movement and services, despite it not necessarily requiring local labor for construction.

title: Soap ad case: HC’s relief for HUL, Wipro
summary: The Bombay High Court has granted interim relief to Hindustan Unilever (HUL) and Wipro Enterprises in a legal battle against USV over an ad campaign for soaps. The court restrained USV from airing ads that disparaged HUL products like Lux, Dove, Pears, and Rin, and also from infringing Wipro's 'Santoor' trademark. The court found USV's product not comparable to soaps and its campaign disparaging, but stayed its order for four weeks at USV's request.

title: Thousands of swing chairs recalled after reports of chair collapsing, tipping over
summary: TJX Companies Inc. is recalling over 30,000 nest swing egg chairs sold under the Tommy Bahama and Martha Stewart brands due to a fall hazard. There have been 27 reports of chairs collapsing or tipping, resulting in 19 injuries including cuts, broken ribs, and a collapsed lung. Consumers are advised to stop using the chairs and return them to Marshalls, T.J. Maxx, HomeGoods, or Homesense stores for a full refund or store gift card.

summary: Olema Oncology is developing OP-1250, a selective ER degrader (SERD) and complete estrogen receptor (ER) antagonist, to treat advanced breast cancer. The company is progressing quickly towards Phase II trials, believing its approach will advance treatment for ER+, HER2- breast cancer.

summary: Jessica Graziano, United Rentals' executive vice president and chief financial officer, will leave the company on July 29, 2022, to join United States Steel Corp. as senior vice president and chief financial officer. Ted Grace has been appointed interim chief financial officer for United Rentals, with CEO Matthew Flannery anticipating a seamless transition. Graziano had been with United Rentals since 2014 and CFO since 2018.

title: Kettering University Class of 2022 graduates at Atwood Stadium
summary: Kettering University's Class of 2022, comprising 375 students, graduated at Atwood Stadium in Flint, Michigan. The commencement ceremony featured alumnus Brady Ericson as the speaker, who encouraged graduates to be curious, take risks, and reflect on their achievements. Paul Sheridan, a graduate receiving his Master of Science in Lean Manufacturing, expressed satisfaction in completing his degree and hopes to apply his new skills to improve productivity in manufacturing.

summary: A House oversight committee is seeking a federal investigation into HCA Healthcare's emergency department admissions practices due to allegations of widespread fraud and that the company admits patients who don't necessarily need emergency care. The inquiry is driven by complaints from workers and concerns about private equity's role in health care, especially given HCA's previous $631 million settlement for false claims. HCA, which turned a profit of almost $7 billion in 2021, states it is reviewing the letter and believes its operational processes are sound.

title: Hormel Foods Unveils "The Inspired People Plaza" and 25-Foot-Tall Sculpture by International Artist Gordon Huether
summary: Hormel Foods unveiled "The Inspired People Plaza" at its global headquarters in Austin, Minn., featuring a 25-foot-tall, 1-ton fork sculpture clad with nearly 20,000 forks donated by team members worldwide. summary: Intuitive Machines, a leading space exploration company, announced its plan to list on Nasdaq through a merger with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. This merger is expected to give Intuitive Machines a pro forma equity value of over $1 billion and will fund its business plan to profitability over the next 2-3 years. The company plays a critical role in NASA's Artemis program, aiming to return the United States to the Moon.

title: Blumenthal calls for investigation into M&T Bank-People's United conversion after 'chaos'
summary: U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal is calling for an investigation by the Federal Reserve and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau into M&T Bank's conversion of People's United accounts after numerous customer complaints about lack of access to funds and poor customer service. This call follows concerns raised by Connecticut Attorney General William Tong regarding a "serious lack of preparation" in the conversion process. The issues have led to significant customer frustration and potential for higher-than-normal customer churn for M&T Bank.

title: Gartner Survey Reveals Talent is Top Challenge Facing CFOs Through 2023
summary: A Gartner survey found that hiring and retaining staff is the top challenge facing CFOs through 2023, with 50% of respondents identifying it as their most difficult task. This talent crunch, alongside persistent inflation and supply chain disruptions, is impacting corporate profitability. Other significant challenges for CFOs include accurate forecasting and cost management.

title: Johnson & Johnson Vision announces €100m investment in Limerick
summary: Johnson & Johnson Vision Care Ireland UC announced a €100 million investment to expand its existing facility in Limerick, Ireland. This expansion aims to create 80 new jobs and increase manufacturing capacity for its ACUVUE® Astigmatism product family and future product pipeline. Production is expected to commence in 2024, reinforcing the company's commitment to the Irish MedTech sector and global eye health.

summary: The Real Brokerage Inc. has appointed Dre Madden as its new Chief Marketing Officer (CMO). title: Lanvin Group to open stores, hunt buys after U.S. SPAC listing
summary: Chinese luxury fashion conglomerate Lanvin Group plans to open 200 new stores globally by 2025 and is seeking new acquisitions following its $150 million New York SPAC listing, which valued the company at $1.31 billion. title: Unilever says litigation with Ben & Jerry's board has 'been resolved'
summary: Unilever announced that its litigation with the independent board of Ben & Jerry's regarding the sale of its Israeli ice cream business has been resolved. The company did not disclose the terms of the resolution. The lawsuit was filed after Ben & Jerry's sought to block Unilever's sale of its Israeli business to local licensee Avi Zinger, citing the brand's values regarding sales in the occupied West Bank.

title: Brazilian airline workers union to go on partial strike from Monday
summary: Brazilian pilots and flight attendants have voted for a partial strike set to begin on Monday, December 19th, demanding a 5% salary increase along with a 5.9% raise to cover inflation. The stoppages will occur daily between 6 a.m. and 8 a.m. at major airports, though flights for medical purposes will be exempt. Airlines Azul, LATAM, and Gol have not yet agreed to the pay demands beyond inflation.

summary: Guardant Health Inc. experienced its largest single-day drop after the results of its colorectal cancer blood test study disappointed investors. Rival company Exact Sciences Corp., which offers a more accurate stool sample test, saw its shares rise significantly.

summary: JELD-WEN Holding, Inc. has announced the appointment of William (Bill) J. Christensen as its new CEO, effective immediately. summary: China is reportedly obstructing the laying and maintenance of submarine internet cables in the South China Sea, delaying projects like the Southeast Asia-Japan Cable 2 (SJC2) for over a year. This obstruction is seen as an attempt by China to control transnational telecommunications infrastructure and prevent foreign surveillance, raising concerns about international maritime law and freedom of navigation.

summary: Robert Half has promoted Ryan Sutton to executive director of its technology practice group. title: Pepperidge Farm releases new cookies inspired by Charleston's Rainbow Row
summary: Pepperidge Farm has launched new Soft Baked Charleston Birthday Cake Cookies, taking inspiration from Charleston's Rainbow Row. summary: Viasat announced that its in-flight connectivity solution will be installed on over 1,000 additional Delta Air Lines aircraft, including widebody fleets (Airbus A330, A350, Boeing 767) and upcoming deliveries (Airbus A220, Boeing 737 MAX). title: enCore Energy commences work to restart production at second South Texas uranium processing plant
summary: enCore Energy Corp announced its decision to restart uranium production at its Alta Mesa Processing Plant in early 2024, making it the company's second producing location following the Rosita Uranium Processing Plant. The Alta Mesa plant, with a capacity of 1.5 million pounds U3O8 per year, will utilize In-Situ Recovery (ISR) technology and is located in Texas. This move aims to cement enCore Energy's position as a leader in US ISR uranium production and provide a reliable domestic low-carbon energy source.

title: Cummins announces Mary Chandler retiring after serving Cummins and its global communities since 2011
summary: Mary Chandler, Vice President – Corporate Responsibility and Community Relations and CEO of the Cummins Foundation, is retiring after 12 years of service. Jim Schacht, currently a member of the Corporate Responsibility Leadership Team, will succeed her, effective April 1. Chandler was instrumental in creating and advancing four global strategic community programs focused on Cummins’ priority areas.

title: Kellogg's announces names for its new companies
summary: The Kellogg Company announced the names for its two new planned companies as it moves forward with its split, expected to be finalized by the end of 2023. The North American cereal business will be named WK Kellogg Co, honoring its founder, while the global snacking, international cereals, noodles, plant-based foods, and North American frozen breakfast foods business will be named Kellanova. title: Thetius Study Highlights Clear Emissions Reduction Advantages of e1 Marine’s Methanol to Hydrogen Fuel Cell Technology
summary: A study by maritime research house Thetius reveals that e1 Marine’s methanol to hydrogen generator technology can significantly reduce emissions in inland waterway vessels. The technology achieves up to 99% reduction in EPA-regulated emissions using grey methanol and up to 85% reduction in GHG emissions with green methanol, offering a viable solution for the maritime industry to meet stringent emissions goals. This innovation is presented as a means to future-proof vessels against escalating environmental regulations and provide a pathway to compliance.

While analyst Chelsey Tam sees potential for near-term share price mutedness due to IPO delays, she also notes Wu's strong technology background could benefit the cloud business.

title: Alibaba’s ex-CEO quits as Jack Ma’s lieutenants take helm
summary: Daniel Zhang has resigned as head of Alibaba's cloud computing unit, a surprise move as Jack Ma's close confidantes, Eddie Wu and Joseph Tsai, take over leadership roles at the company. title: Barrick Gold drills in Dominican Republic as part of earn-in agreement
summary: Barrick Gold Corporation has begun drilling in the Lithocap Zone of Precipitate Gold's Pueblo Grande Project in the Dominican Republic. This initiative is part of an earn-in agreement enabling Barrick to acquire a 70% stake by investing $10 million over six years and conducting 7,500 meters of drilling. The program aims to explore for gold and potentially deeper copper, expanding on previous discoveries in the nearby Pueblo Viejo mining operation.

title: Empresas Copec, Banco de Chile y Entel son las marcas más valiosas de Chile según Brand Finance
summary: A Brand Finance report identifies Empresas Copec, Banco de Chile, and Entel as the most valuable brands in Chile. Empresas Copec leads the ranking with a value of USD1.5 billion, while Banco de Chile and Entel follow closely with USD1.3 billion and USD1.0 billion, respectively. Entel is also recognized as the strongest brand, and Jumbo showed the most significant growth.

summary: The federal government has mandated that Rogers Communications Inc. open its Toronto subway cellular network to BCE Inc. and Telus Corp. by October 3rd, 2023. This decision comes after months of deadlock between the companies regarding technical and financial terms for providing wireless services to all TTC riders. Industry Minister François-Philippe Champagne emphasized that carriers have a collective responsibility and failure to meet the deadlines could result in penalties.

summary: Activist investor Starboard Value, a significant shareholder in Bloomin' Brands, has hired industry veteran Dave George as an advisor to help with a turnaround effort. George, known for his work at Darden Restaurants, including LongHorn Steakhouse and Olive Garden, will assist in improving Bloomin' Brands, parent company of Outback Steakhouse. summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved the reappointment of Sandeep Bakhshi as the Managing Director and CEO of ICICI Bank Limited for a three-year term, from October 4, 2023, to October 3, 2026. Bakhshi has been with the ICICI Group since 1986 and assumed the MD & CEO role in October 2018.

title: Pune: COEP Alumni to Receive Coveted Abhiman Award from Maharashtra Minister
summary: COEP Technological University will be presenting the 'COEP Abhiman Award' to its alumni who have excelled in various fields. The awards will be bestowed by the Minister of Higher and Technical Education of Maharashtra, Chandrakant Patil, at a ceremony on September 14th. Notable awardees include IPS Vivek Phansalkar, Arun Kudale, Chetan Dharia, Ravi Bhatkal, Vijay Patel, and Ashish Achlerkar.

title: Mining Law Reform Neglects Mine Closure Process
summary: The Mining Law reform, enacted in May 2023, has introduced significant uncertainty in the Mexican mining sector, particularly regarding mine closure procedures. Marisol Barragán of New Gold highlights that while the law mandates a "Mining Restoration, Closure and Post-Closure Program," it currently lacks specific steps for implementation and clear evaluation criteria. The industry awaits further rules from the government, expected within 180 days of the law's publication, to provide much-needed clarity and avoid ongoing uncertainty.

summary: First Advantage, an Atlanta-based company, has acquired Infinite ID, a biometrics company that was a portfolio company of Chevy Chase's Enlightenment Capital, for $41 million. title: J.M. Smucker to Purchase Hostess Brands in $5.6 Billion Deal
summary: J.M. Smucker Co. is acquiring Hostess Brands for $5.6 billion, including debt, aiming to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing snack market. This strategic move is expected to enhance Smucker's presence in the convenience store channel and meet the increasing consumer demand for on-the-go snack options. Hostess, known for Twinkies and Ding Dongs, has a history of financial struggles but its acquisition aligns with Smucker's ongoing diversification into various consumer goods sectors like coffee and pet food.

title: SEC charges Fluor with improper accounting and inadequate internal accounting controls
summary: The SEC has brought settled charges against Fluor Corporation for improper accounting and inadequate internal accounting controls related to two large-scale, fixed-price construction projects. The company allegedly overstated its net earnings due to non-compliance with percentage-of-completion accounting under GAAP, leading to a restatement. Fluor agreed to pay a $14.5 million civil penalty, and five officers and employees were also charged with individual penalties.

title: Wiz and Fortinet announce partnership to deliver cloud-native security protection
summary: Wiz and Fortinet have partnered to enhance cloud infrastructure and workload security for their joint customers. The integration allows Wiz's Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) to identify network exposure risks and toxic combinations, which the Fortinet Security Fabric then uses to create automated security enforcement with FortiGate Firewall. This collaboration enables customers to automatically detect and remediate unwanted public exposures, respond to real-time threats, and remove exposures based on business impact.

title: Blue Buffalo expects flat pet food sales in Q1 FY24
summary: General Mills expects its Pet segment, including Blue Buffalo, to report roughly flat organic net sales in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024, with an operating profit margin of approximately 19 percent. This moderation is attributed to increasing caution among U.S. pet parents, who are shifting towards value-oriented products and smaller pack sizes, and a negative impact on treats and wet food due to pet parents spending more time away from home. Despite these short-term challenges, General Mills sees strong long-term growth opportunities for Blue Buffalo due to the ongoing pet humanization trend.

title: The Allure of Tax-Free Municipal Bonds
summary: This article highlights the benefits of tax-free municipal bonds, especially for high earners in states with high income taxes. It explains the varying state income tax landscapes across the U.S. and positions municipal bonds as a steady, lower-risk investment option with significant tax advantages. The author also introduces the Near-Term Tax Free Fund (NEARX) managed by U.S. Global Investors as a recommended investment vehicle for those interested in tax-free municipal bonds.

summary: Former Qualcomm Technologies CEO Paul Jacobs has been named the new CEO of Globalstar, coinciding with a licensing agreement that gives Globalstar exclusive access to certain XCOM Labs technologies and personnel. This deal, valued at approximately $63.6 million, aims to leverage Globalstar's terrestrial spectrum with XCOM's high-performance wireless technology. The move is expected to drive innovation in satellite communications and enhance value for Globalstar shareholders.

title: An Introduction to AI in 5G and 6G
summary: This article explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into 5G and future 6G wireless networks. It highlights how AI is already being studied for 5G advancements by 3GPP and O-RAN ALLIANCE, focusing on areas like network energy saving, load balancing, and orchestration. For 6G, the article emphasizes the concept of "AI-native" networks, where AI would be fundamental to all aspects, including potentially designing entire air interfaces and optimizing network management on city-wide or national scales.

title: The hottest back-to-school accessory? A location sharing app
summary: Location sharing apps are becoming increasingly popular among American families, with Life360 reporting a significant surge in sign-ups this year. While many parents use these apps to track their children for safety, especially as kids gain independence, experts debate whether this constant surveillance truly reduces anxiety or hinders a child's development of self-reliance. Life360's founder, Chris Hulls, was inspired to create the app after Hurricane Katrina highlighted the need for family tracking technology, aiming to provide peace of mind for loved ones.

Additionally, Magna is developing new door carriers using natural fibers and plant-based polyurethanes, making them lighter, more sustainable, and less energy-intensive to produce.

title: Altria Seeks Refund Suit Stay While Supreme Court Considers Moore
summary: Altria Group Inc. has filed an unopposed motion to stay its refund suit against the United States, pending a decision by the Supreme Court in Moore v. United States. Altria asserts that a ruling in Moore, which addresses whether the Sixteenth Amendment allows taxation of unrealized sums without apportionment, will be binding authority on its own case, where it claims to have been unconstitutionally taxed on unrealized income. The stay is requested to promote judicial economy by avoiding duplicative litigation and allowing time for resolutions in other issues.

title: Neurocrine Biosciences Announces Initiation of Phase 1 Clinical Study Evaluating Effects of NBI-1117570 in Healthy Adults
summary: Neurocrine Biosciences has started a Phase 1 clinical study for NBI-1117570, an oral, muscarinic M1/M4 selective dual agonist. This investigational compound is being evaluated for its safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics in healthy adults. The company believes NBI-1117570 has the potential to treat neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions by targeting M1 and M4 receptors, which are involved in cognition and psychosis.

Vinai, named after the Thai refugee camp where Vang was born, aims for a spring 2024 opening and will tell the story of his Hmong American heritage through food.

title: Newmark Completes $45 Million Sale of One Liberty Square in Downtown Boston, Massachusetts
summary: Newmark has announced the $45 million sale of One Liberty Square, a 157,467-square-foot LEED Gold-certified office/retail asset in Downtown Boston. The transaction, which involved Clarion Partners as the seller and Synergy Investments as the buyer, represents the largest office sale in Downtown Boston since the first quarter of 2022. title: SAGE
summary: The SAGE (Semi-Automatic Ground Environment) project was a monumental bi-product of the cold war, beginning in 1949 after the Soviet Union detonated its first atomic bomb. The system, developed by a collaboration of innovative US entities led by MIT's Lincoln Laboratories, became the largest computer project of its time and a significant turning point for IBM, contributing 80% to its computing revenue between 1952 and 1955. SAGE pioneered many technologies such as magnetic core memories, the first real-time operating system, and CRT terminals with light pens, which laid the groundwork for future computing advancements and products like Sabre, the IBM 704, Fortran, and the IBM System/360.

summary: Conagra Brands, Inc. has completed the sale of its 51.8% ownership stake in Agro Tech Foods Ltd., an Indian food company. This sale means Conagra will no longer include Agro Tech Foods' results in its financial statements. Funds advised by Convergent Finance LLP and Samara Capital acquired the stake, with Agro Tech Foods continuing to license the ACT II brand from Conagra for use in India.

title: How Trump’s Justice Dept. Derailed an Investigation of a Major Company (Published 2024)
summary: A federal criminal investigation into Caterpillar for alleged tax avoidance was significantly hampered, leading to its closure without criminal charges or substantial penalties, partly due to the company's hiring of well-connected lawyers, including William P. Barr. A planned interview with a key witness in Amsterdam was abruptly canceled by the Justice Department, and records seized from the company were never reviewed by agents. The IRS ultimately sought less than a quarter of the back taxes initially claimed, highlighting the raw legal power deployed by Caterpillar.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) Reports Solid Earnings Growth in Q2 Fiscal 2024
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) reported strong financial results for Q2 fiscal 2024, with net sales increasing by 5.7% to $57.33 billion and net income rising to $1.743 billion. The company saw significant growth in membership fees and e-commerce, with e-commerce sales up 18.4%. Costco continues to expand its global footprint with 875 warehouses worldwide, demonstrating a resilient business model and effective strategy in a competitive retail environment.

title: Home Depot in new partnership to enhance retail media network
summary: The Home Depot is partnering with Pentaleap Inc. to upgrade its Orange Apron Media retail media network, aiming to improve the shopping experience and return on ad spend for suppliers. This collaboration leverages Pentaleap's Fluid Relevancy Engine to more effectively target ads to customers, enhancing both customer satisfaction and advertiser experience. Home Depot initiated its retail media network in 2018, upgrading it to Orange Apron Media in March 2024, and it is now the largest home improvement offering of its kind.

title: Philip Morris International does not give up on cigarettes and opens a factory in Tanzania
summary: Philip Morris International (PMI) is expanding its market for smoked cigarettes in low- and middle-income countries by promoting tobacco cultivation and opening a cigarette factory in Tanzania. This move contradicts PMI's public claims of working towards "a smoke-free world" and its investments in new tobacco products. Tanzania, despite ratifying the FCTC, remains heavily influenced by the tobacco industry, with its government actively supporting tobacco production.

title: Activist Petrus Advisers has a plan to help lift Criteo’s share price. Here’s how it might unfold
summary: Activist investor Petrus Advisers has outlined a plan to boost Criteo's share price, proposing actions such as an investor day, accelerating share buybacks, and a strategic review. The firm, holding a 5.60% stake, also calls for board refreshment. This comes as Criteo faces challenges from the phasing out of third-party cookies and communication issues with investors, despite strong performance in its retail media segment.

title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims on Behalf of Investors of Mister Car Wash, Inc. - MCW
summary: Pomerantz LLP is investigating potential securities fraud claims against Mister Car Wash, Inc. (MCW) on behalf of its investors. This investigation follows MCW's announcement of Q4 and fiscal year 2023 financial results, where revenue missed consensus estimates by $0.32 million, leading to a 10.34% stock price drop. Investors are encouraged to contact Pomerantz LLP for more information about joining a potential class action lawsuit.

title: Southwest delays over 800 flights, over 150 canceled during Spring Break travel
summary: Southwest Airlines experienced significant delays and cancellations during the start of Spring Break travel, with over 800 flights delayed and 159 canceled nationwide on March 9. The disruptions were attributed to thunderstorms in the Southeast. At Indianapolis International Airport, 38 Southwest flights were delayed and eight canceled, causing frustration for travelers planning vacations.

summary: Megacap tech stocks frequently dominate ESG funds because these funds still aim for top performers within economic groups, and the tech sector is considered "cleaner" regarding environmental impact. summary: Applied Materials has inaugurated its 'India Validation Center' (IVC) in Bangalore, marking a significant step in developing India's semiconductor ecosystem. The center, commissioned by Union Cabinet Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, aims to enable early pilot programs, talent development, and advanced capabilities for semiconductor equipment design and qualification, including processing 300-mm wafers. This initiative is expected to strengthen India's chip manufacturing resilience and support the country's semiconductor industry.

title: Huawei chip used tech from two US gear suppliers
summary: Last year, Huawei Technologies Co. and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. (SMIC) utilized U.S. technology from Applied Materials Inc. and Lam Research Corp. to produce an advanced 7-nanometer chip in China. This highlights China's ongoing reliance on foreign components for cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing. Despite the chip powering Huawei's Mate 60 Pro and being celebrated in China, the machinery used to produce it included technology from Dutch maker ASML Holding NV, as well as the U.S. gear, acquired before Washington banned such sales to China in October 2022.

title: Grilled cheese and tomato soup is Campbell's 1st-ever, limited-edition flavor
summary: Campbell's has released its first-ever limited-edition flavor: grilled cheese and tomato soup, honoring National Grilled Cheese Day on April 12. The soup can be prepared with water for a robust tomato taste or milk for a cheesier flavor. Campbell's is also running a sweepstakes through March 20, 2024, giving away 412 cans to celebrate the new offering.

summary: The Dimensional U.S. Small Cap ETF (DFAS) aims to maximize after-tax value and has outperformed its benchmark, the Russell 2000, on a pre-tax basis despite a market focus on growth stocks. Riley Financial, Inc. summary: JGT2 Redevelopment is revitalizing the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay, Maine, which includes 1,000 acres, 1.4 million square feet of buildings, and a 150-megawatt power plant. The project involves developing a 75 MW solar farm and utilizing three 50 MW gas turbine generators for peak power. Additionally, the redevelopment will host Godfrey Forest Products' new OSB plant and retain one million square feet of industrial space for various businesses, leveraging renewable energy and strong infrastructure.

summary: Moose Toys has expanded its senior leadership team by hiring four experienced toy industry veterans: John Coyne, Craig Drobis, Deirdre Cross, and Stephen Davis. summary: Tilman Fertitta, billionaire owner of Landry’s Inc. and the Houston Rockets, has upgraded to a new $150 million, 252-foot Feadship superyacht named Boardwalk. summary: Keysight Technologies and Ericsson have successfully demonstrated a prototype for an early 6G network. This collaboration involves Ericsson's pre-standard protocol stack, designed for new spectrum bands, and Keysight's test system, which emulates user equipment. The initiative aims to evaluate new frequency ranges and address the development challenges of higher spectrum and necessary modifications to the 5G protocol stack for future 6G applications.

summary: Rich Foster, VP of L3Harris Technologies Canada, delivered a speech at CANSEC addressing the urgent need for industry and government to adapt to evolving geopolitical, technological, and environmental challenges. He emphasized the importance of collaboration, suggesting changes to procurement processes, strategic integration with the U.S. supply chain, and focused long-term R&D investment within Canada to enhance national security and competitiveness. Foster urged a more decisive approach given current global conflicts and threats.

title: LivaNova Misses Primary Endpoint in RECOVER Clinical Study
summary: LivaNova's VNS Therapy study for treatment-resistant depression in unipolar patients did not achieve its primary endpoint, though it did show statistical significance in select secondary endpoints. The failure to meet the primary endpoint was attributed to an unexpectedly strong response in the sham group. Despite this, LivaNova believes the overall data supports a meaningful treatment effect and plans to publish the detailed results in 4Q24.

title: Polaris Project Gives EV Off-Roaders Places To Plug In
summary: Polaris Inc. has launched a pilot program in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, installing four remote charging stations for electric off-road vehicles along 100 miles of trails. This initiative, supported by a $700,000 grant, aims to address the challenge of range anxiety for EV off-roaders and provide crucial charging infrastructure in remote areas. The program also includes an all-electric rental experience for the Polaris Ranger XP Kinetic, introducing new customers to EV off-roading and gathering data on vehicle performance and charging needs in challenging environments.

summary: TransDigm Group Inc. has completed its $1.4 billion cash acquisition of Communications & Power Industries’ (CPI) Electron Device business. This acquisition, first announced in November, focuses on electronic components and subsystems primarily for the aerospace and defense sector. The acquired business generated approximately $300 million in sales for the fiscal year ending September 29, 2023, with a significant 70% of its revenue coming from the aftermarket.

title: AbbVie's tight grip on Humira market raises concerns about biosimilars
summary: AbbVie's top-selling arthritis drug Humira has maintained over 80% of its patient base despite facing nine lower-priced biosimilar rivals in the U.S. market, raising concerns among drug pricing experts and analysts about the viability of the biosimilar market. Industry middlemen, pharmacy benefit managers, have largely dictated patient access to these biosimilars, offering little incentive for doctors to switch. Regulatory reform is being advocated to make biosimilars more accessible to patients and encourage their development, as significant potential savings have been lost.

title: Crypto Marketplace Bakkt Weighs Potential Sale, Breakup
summary: Bakkt Holdings Inc., a digital-asset marketplace established by the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is reportedly considering strategic options including a potential sale or breakup. This exploration comes amidst heightened merger and acquisition activity in the crypto sector and after Bakkt issued a "going concern" warning earlier in the year. The company is working with a financial advisor, but no final decision has been reached, and remaining independent is still an option.

title: COVID shots should target JN.1 variant in fall 2024 campaign, US FDA says
summary: The U.S. FDA has advised COVID-19 vaccine manufacturers to target the JN.1 variant for the fall 2024 vaccination campaign, aligning with European and WHO recommendations. This decision comes despite newer strains now being more prevalent, partly because Novavax can only target the older JN.1 variant. Moderna and Pfizer/BioNTech are also preparing updated vaccines for the JN.1 strain, but vaccine uptake has been a concern, with only about 22.5% of U.S. adults receiving a COVID shot in the previous season.

title: Attorney general intervenes on Consumers Energy case requesting $303M rate increase
summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel has intervened in Consumers Energy's request for a $303 million annual electricity rate increase, which would raise rates by 6.5% starting in March 2025. Nessel's office scrutinizes such filings to protect customers from unjustifiable costs, noting the company previously received a $92 million increase this year after requesting $216 million. Consumers Energy argues the increase is necessary to fund a $7 billion distribution plan aimed at improving reliability through infrastructure upgrades and maintenance, citing potential 40% cost savings by investing now rather than reacting to failures later.

title: General Mills Sued Over Racial Discrimination Claims in Georgia
summary: Eight Black employees have filed a class-action lawsuit against General Mills, alleging racial discrimination from white managers at their Georgia manufacturing plant. The lawsuit details a hostile work environment, including the use of Confederate imagery and racial slurs, and claims human resources ignored past complaints. The plaintiffs are seeking monetary relief and the dismissal of "racist decisionmakers."

title: HF Foods to pay $3.9M to settle execs’ alleged fraud
summary: HF Foods Group has agreed to pay a $3.9 million penalty to settle alleged fraudulent conduct by its former chief executive officer and chief financial officer. The SEC accused the former executives, Zhou Min Ni and Jian Ming Ni, of misappropriating approximately $3.4 million and scheming to remove $7.4 million in liabilities from a predecessor company's books. Zhou Min Ni will pay a $300,000 penalty and Jian Ming Ni $80,000 in their individual settlements.

title: RVLV Announces Permanent Aspen Store Location as First Brick and Mortar Following Successful Pop-Up Experience
summary: Revolve Group (RVLV) has announced the opening of its first permanent physical retail store in Aspen, Colorado, following the success of a pop-up experience in the same location. The new store will house collections from both REVOLVE and FWRD, offering apparel, footwear, and accessories, and aims to blend online and offline shopping experiences for Millennial and Generation Z consumers. This move leverages Aspen's luxury market and will include regular in-store events and trunk shows.

title: SDPD first in county to upgrade to latest TASER 10, giving them further range with less voltage
summary: The San Diego Police Department is the first in San Diego County to upgrade to the new TASER 10 energy weapon by Axon Enterprise Inc. This new model offers a longer range of 45 feet, uses less voltage, and features 10 probes, improving effectiveness in non-lethal de-escalation situations. The upgrade, costing $1.95 million for the first year, is part of a five-year agreement and will be rolled out to 1,860 officers starting in Fall 2024.

title: TSMC-backed VIS joint venture confirms construction of S$10.5 billion chip plant in S'pore
summary: Vanguard International Semiconductor (VIS) and NXP Semiconductors NV are establishing a S$10.5 billion chip plant in Singapore, a joint venture that will begin construction in late 2024 and production in 2027. While not producing cutting-edge chips, the facility will address high demand for automotive and industrial chips, contributing to supply chain diversification and creating 1,500 jobs. Singapore was chosen due to its skilled workforce and previous successful collaborations between the companies.

title: Labor union says Enbridge Gas to cut emergency response shifts in Toronto
summary: Canadian labor union Unifor announced that Enbridge Gas plans to cut emergency response shifts in Toronto to curtail costs. The union argues that reducing evening and overnight shifts and compliance tasks will increase the risk of gas incidents and urged local government agencies to review the company's contracts. Enbridge Gas denies a lack of employees for emergency response and is engaging with Unifor on the issue.

title: TotalEnergies and Air Products sign deal for green hydrogen delivery
summary: TotalEnergies and Air Products have signed a 15-year agreement for the annual supply of 70,000 tons of green hydrogen in Europe starting in 2030. This deal supports TotalEnergies' goal to cut net emissions by 40% by 2030 and includes a power purchase agreement for TotalEnergies to supply Air Products with 150 megawatts of solar power. The companies are also exploring further renewable energy collaboration in Britain, Poland, and France.

title: Humana can challenge Medicare clawback rule in Fort Worth, Texas - judge
summary: A federal judge in Fort Worth, Texas, ruled that Humana's lawsuit challenging a Biden administration rule allowing Medicare to reclaim billions from insurers for overcharges can proceed. The judge rejected the administration's request to dismiss the case or transfer it to Dallas, stating that arguments for transfer were not supported. Humana claims the rule is "arbitrary and capricious" and could have "unpredictable consequences" for Medicare Advantage organizations and beneficiaries.

summary: Aptiv PLC (APTV) leverages its "smart architecture" and frequent acquisitions to capitalize on the connected cars market, despite increasing costs from investments and legal matters. Aptiv's strategy focuses on electrification, connectivity, and autonomy trends in the automotive sector, driving both organic and inorganic growth.

summary: Abbott has launched its over-the-counter continuous glucose monitoring system, Lingo, in the U.S., making it the second such device on the market for adults not on insulin. Abbott received U.S. health regulator clearance for Lingo in June and plans extensive marketing.

McMullen testified in federal court, stating the merger would allow Kroger to lower prices and better compete with larger retailers like Walmart and Amazon.

title: Konieczny named CEO at Amcor
summary: Amcor plc has appointed Peter Konieczny as its permanent CEO, removing his interim title. Konieczny, who previously served as chief commercial officer, took over as interim CEO in April after the former CEO retired for health reasons. The board expressed confidence in Konieczny's leadership, citing his exceptional performance and role in strengthening the company's financial results during his interim tenure.

title: New Clinical Data Validates Vor Bio’s Approach of Using Shielded Transplants to Deliver Targeted Therapies
summary: Vor Bio announced new clinical data from its Phase 1/2 VBP101 study, demonstrating that trem-cel combined with Mylotarg showed reliable engraftment, shielding from toxicity, a broadened therapeutic window, and early patient benefit in relapsed/refractory AML. The company is also advancing VCAR33 ALLO for AML and introducing a new preclinical asset, VADC45, with potential applications across oncology, gene therapy, and autoimmune disorders. Vor Bio plans to discuss pivotal trial designs for trem-cel + Mylotarg with the FDA by year-end.

This deal aims to strengthen Gilead's pipeline, complementing its other strategic acquisitions and partnerships in oncology and HIV.

title: Columbia County coal plant retirement delayed for a second time, now pushed to 2029
summary: The retirement of the Columbia Energy Center, a coal-fired power plant in Columbia County, has been delayed until 2029 for the second time. Co-owner utilities, including Alliant Energy, Madison Gas and Electric, and Wisconsin Public Service, stated this delay allows time to explore converting the plant to natural gas to ensure reliability and meet demand. Environmental groups like Clean Wisconsin criticize the delay, arguing it locks the region into more fossil fuel burning and that natural gas, while cleaner than coal, still contributes significantly to climate change through methane emissions.

summary: Bank of America has maintained an Underperform rating on Intel Corporation (INTC) and sees an increased likelihood of a business separation following CEO Pat Gelsinger's unexpected retirement. This assessment comes amidst Intel's IDM 2.0 strategy not yielding desired results and highlights the competitive issues both divisions face.

title: Freight giant CSX’s US Supreme Court appeal tests reach of antitrust law
summary: Freight rail giant CSX has appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court, seeking to revive its lawsuit against Norfolk Southern for allegedly denying access to a key East Coast terminal and costing CSX hundreds of millions in lost profits. CSX argues that a U.S. appeals court wrongly dismissed its antitrust claims, asserting that the "continuing-violation doctrine" should apply given Norfolk Southern's ongoing practice of overcharging for terminal access. The Supreme Court's decision on whether to hear the appeal could clarify the application of this doctrine in antitrust law.

title: CMS enters agreement with Vertex, bluebird to improve access to gene therapies
summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has reached "outcomes-based agreements" with Vertex Pharmaceuticals and bluebird bio aimed at increasing patient access to their gene therapies for sickle cell disease. These agreements will tie payments to the therapies' effectiveness in improving health outcomes for patients enrolled in Medicaid, providing state Medicaid agencies with more budget predictability for these high-cost treatments. The initiative addresses the slow uptake of these gene therapies (Lyfgenia and Casgevy), which have U.S. list prices of $2.2 million and $3.1 million respectively, and primarily impact over 100,000 people in the U.S., many of whom are Black and enrolled in Medicaid.

While the drug, combined with chemotherapy, significantly improved progression-free survival, it did not achieve a statistically significant benefit in overall survival, which is a key requirement for FDA approval. Despite this, some Wall Street analysts remain optimistic, speculating that more follow-up data might clarify the overall survival benefit.

title: Synopsys suspends China sales; Ansys merger gets FTC nod
summary: Synopsys has suspended all sales to China due to new trade restrictions from the Trump administration, impacting a market that accounts for about 10% of its revenues. title: Groundbreaking ASCO Data: Novel BCL-2 Inhibitor Defeats Drug Resistance in Advanced Blood Cancer
